# Agent client compatibility

UADOS provides a common project record and lifecycle through [MASTER_AGENT_WORKFLOW.md](../MASTER_AGENT_WORKFLOW.md). Its native entry files request explicit reading of that authority; this is a compatibility contract, not proof that a product obeyed it. No provider credentials, hidden API calls or commercial client launch are required by the local CLI.

Official loader documentation was checked on **2026-10-12**. Loader behavior can change; recheck product documentation when upgrading.

| Client | UADOS entry | Documented discovery and relevant limit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Codex | Root `AGENTS.md` | Loads instructions from root toward working directory; `AGENTS.override.md` and configured fallbacks can take precedence. Combined project instructions default to a 32 KiB limit. Keep this adapter short and explicitly read the master. [Official documentation](https://developers.openai.com/codex/guides/agents-md) |
| Claude Code | Root `CLAUDE.md` importing `@MASTER_AGENT_WORKFLOW.md` | Markdown imports are supported. Native `AGENTS.md` discovery is version/settings dependent; the supplied CLAUDE entry avoids relying on it. If import is unavailable, read the master explicitly. [Official documentation](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory) |
| Cursor | `.cursor/rules/uados.mdc` | Project rules use `.mdc` with frontmatter; plain `.md` in this directory is ignored. `alwaysApply: true` activates the wrapper. Referenced files are not automatically inlined, so its body instructs an explicit read. Root `AGENTS.md` is also supported. [Official documentation](https://cursor.com/docs/rules) |
| Qoder | Root `AGENTS.md` | Automatically recognizes AGENTS. Native `.qoder/rules` take precedence on conflicts; active rule content has a combined size limit. The entry uses a plain file path and explicit read instruction, not an assumed import. [Official documentation](https://docs.qoder.com/user-guide/rules) |
| ZCode | Root `AGENTS.md` | Documents global and workspace AGENTS sources. CLAUDE migration is onboarding behavior, not continuous runtime loading. This contract does not assume nested discovery, imports or a shared merge algorithm. [Official documentation](https://zcode.z.ai/en/docs/agents) |

Adapters do not duplicate lifecycle rules. `.cursor/rules/uados.md` remains a portable human reference alongside the actual `.mdc` wrapper. Native product instructions may change precedence; inspect them without silently overwriting existing files during adoption.

Role selection produces provider-neutral assignments and a dispatch packet with task/context/instructions. A human or authorized host starts actual independent contributors and supplies their results through the CLI. Capability labels and agent labels are declared metadata, not verified model skills or identity. The team must establish actual independence.

Local validation covers maintained file parity, packaged hidden/nested assets, CLI behavior and simulated identity switching. It does not claim end-to-end execution of Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, Qoder and ZCode. Commercial-client integration, provider dispatch, native hooks, remote authentication and client-specific automated enforcement remain explicit integrations to test.

# Agent handover protocol

Authority: [master workflow, section 6](../MASTER_AGENT_WORKFLOW.md#6-close-with-a-usable-handover). `SESSION_HANDOVER.md` is generated by session closure; this worksheet is preparation material, not an alternative register.

Before closing, assemble current status, completed work with validation, remaining task IDs, known problems, important decision IDs, rejected approaches and recommended next actions. Include paths, exact commands and access/environment constraints needed by a contributor who cannot read the old chat. Distinguish done, submitted for review, blocked and unvalidated work.

Use `session close` with the concise summary and actionable next steps; include actual blockers and failed approaches. Check generated handover and audit. Preserve unfinished implementation artifacts and contributor history. The incoming agent checks the ledger, task leases, evidence fingerprints and resource availability, starts its own stable session and uses the master's context procedure.

A scenario labeled “Day 1 Claude Code → Day 30 Codex” may use logical day labels to test recovery. Such labels do not establish 30 elapsed days or actual commercial-client invocation. Report the simulation method and invocation evidence separately.
documents..agent/memory_update_protocol.md:
# Project memory update protocol

Authority: [master workflow, section 3](../MASTER_AGENT_WORKFLOW.md#3-execute-and-preserve-reasoning). See [PROJECT_MEMORY/README.md](../PROJECT_MEMORY/README.md) for the resource map.

Route a fact to one primary record: task outcome and evidence through task commands; significant choices through decision/change records; experiment execution and interpretation through research commands; technical explanations, lessons and failures through `note` or maintained `PROJECT_MEMORY/notes/`; stopping context through session closure. Keep architecture and policies maintained, with a tracked rationale for significant changes.

A durable note names its task/source, observation date or event, scope, conclusion, evidence strength, uncertainty and affected next decision. Preserve negative results, rejected alternatives and failure triggers. Record resource identifiers and authorized retrieval instructions without credentials or confidential raw data.

Generated views are read-only inputs for contributors. Repair projection drift from the ledger using the master's audit procedure; do not edit the view to make evidence appear consistent. After changing governed maintained memory, refresh affected sessions and inspect the new context report. A content hash supports comparison of bytes; it is not proof of honest observation.
documents..agent/startup_protocol.md:
# Agent startup protocol

Authority: [master workflow, section 1](../MASTER_AGENT_WORKFLOW.md#1-establish-context-before-action). This operational worksheet supports startup without replacing its gates.

Prepare a context packet with stable contributor label, client/runtime name if known, project root, recorded mode, intended task, policy version and current resource access. Inspect mode-detection evidence; distinguish a classification assumption from an observed resource. Read the task and dependencies before proposing parallel work.

The issued `PROJECT UNDERSTANDING REPORT` is the startup output. Verify its objective, phase, architecture, completed work, problems, risks, resource inventory and next actions against their files. Add explicit findings for missing data, unavailable services, resource constraints and unresolved assumptions. Do not fabricate capability or availability from a filename.

Record the exact issued report hash, acknowledge it and prepare the evidence-backed execution plan required for the task's protocol. Keep the report in the generated session register. If tracked state or governed documents change, use the master's refresh/acknowledgement procedure. Read [compatibility.md](compatibility.md) when the client cannot discover these instructions reliably.
documents..agent/task_execution_protocol.md:
# Task execution protocol

Authority: [master workflow, sections 2–4](../MASTER_AGENT_WORKFLOW.md#2-define-and-review-owned-work). Use this worksheet to assemble the task packet; the task's recorded protocol controls its gates.

| Stage | Concrete record or outcome |
| --- | --- |
| Task definition | Observable outcome, acceptance criteria, scopes, dependencies and existing-work inspection |
| Risk assessment | Consequence of failure and why routine/major classification fits |
| Implementation plan | Proposed steps, alternatives, recovery and meaningful validation; readable supporting evidence |
| Multi-agent review | Independent challenge; protocol-2 major role coverage, debate rounds and consensus |
| Execution | Claimed ownership and coherent maintained implementation |
| Validation | Executed commands/procedures, inputs, environment, failures and result evidence |
| Documentation update | Architecture, rationale, lessons and acceptance gaps in their proper maintained/ledger records |
| Final audit | Current consistency result and unresolved findings; current major result approvals before completion |

Review changes with the [debate protocol](../MULTI_AGENT_SYSTEM/debate_protocol.md) and [change policy](../CHANGE_REQUESTS/CHANGE_POLICY.md). A new task plan is a durable record, not a chat-only promise. Keep validation evidence outside generated files and preserve original failures. When a resource or ownership conflict blocks work, record the actual issue and a specific recovery action rather than lowering risk or inventing success.

documents.AUDIT/README.md:
# Audit and recovery

The ledger is authoritative; generated files are readable projections. Audit checks consistency of the stored record and recorded evidence. It cannot establish that a scientific claim is correct or that a collaborator is authentic.

```sh
python -m uados --project . audit
python -m uados --project . audit --repair
```

Use the command's result and diagnostics as the record of what was inspected. `--repair` regenerates projections from a valid ledger. It does not rewrite history, invent missing evidence or restore altered scoped files.

## Recovery decisions

| Observation | Interpretation | Response |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Generated Markdown or JSON differs | Projection drift or interrupted generation | Preserve useful diagnostics, then repair projections and audit again |
| Evidence is missing or changed | The recorded claim cannot be verified against its original artifact | Restore the exact artifact from a trusted backup or rerun validation and record new evidence; obtain a fresh review when needed |
| Ledger hash chain or state is inconsistent | Authoritative-record integrity is uncertain | Stop tracked work, preserve a copy and restore a verified backup; do not “fix” the chain by hand |
| Session context is stale | Recorded state or maintained context changed | Refresh, inspect the new report and acknowledge its hash |
| Conflicting active ownership | Parallel work overlaps or an earlier owner left | Coordinate takeover and record the reason; do not remove a lock or overwrite files blindly |
| Experiment was interrupted | Execution may have partial outputs or a surviving process | Inspect execution state, stop it through an appropriate authorized mechanism if needed, then use `experiment resolve` with the recovery reason before a safe rerun |
| Required resource is unavailable | Validation cannot establish the intended claim | Record a blocker and recovery action; do not call the result empty or passing |

## Locking and interrupted writes

The CLI holds a stable operating-system project lock across record mutation and projection generation. Process exit releases the operating-system lock; the lock file may remain and is not itself evidence that a process still owns it. Do not unlink a lock file to bypass a competing writer, because separate writers could then lock different inodes.

SQLite commits ledger event and current state together. Projection files are generated after that commit and can be rebuilt if generation stops. An interrupted projection write therefore needs regeneration, while a failed database commit needs investigation of the record before further work. If the CLI reports that an event committed but projection generation failed, do not repeat the original action: repair and inspect the committed state first.

## Preservation and restart

Keep a verified backup of ledger, maintained documents and relevant evidence. Before destructive recovery, retain the original files and diagnostics. After restoring, audit, inspect the latest handover and start a new acknowledged session. Revalidate external resources; a copied project does not establish their current availability.

If the local database is absent after a Git clone, `rebuild-ledger` can reconstruct it from a complete validated `.uados/events.jsonl` and matching exported state when present. Preserve a consistent Git revision of memory and evidence as well. The command refuses an existing database; it is not a corruption-overwrite mechanism. If exports disagree, recover a coherent revision instead of editing hashes until validation passes.

When an audit reveals a repeated failure, record a lesson and review a bounded policy improvement using `ENGINEERING_RULES/extensions.md`.

# Independent adversarial review

Date: 2026-10-12 (Asia/Shanghai). Reviewer: `Independent-Design-Reviewer`.

Scope: `src/uados/storage.py`, `context.py`, `project.py`, `research.py`, `cli.py`, and the persisted workflow contracts. The reviewer challenged the proposed architecture before implementation, inspected the runtime independently, and authored `tests/test_adversarial.py`. Runtime fixes were made by the primary implementer. This record describes actual review activity; it does not claim that implementation performed before UADOS bootstrapping was governed by its later CLI gates.

## Verdict

The local, cooperative workflow design is acceptable for v1 delivery after the fixes below. There are no unresolved blocking findings in the reviewed cases. The stated limits remain part of the operating contract, rather than evidence of distributed operation, identity authentication, or complete scientific reproducibility.

## Challenges and verified fixes

| Severity | Failure challenged | Implemented resolution | Verification |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| P0 | Separately replacing a state file and event journal cannot create one atomic commit. | SQLite commits the authoritative state and event together; JSON and Markdown are rebuildable projections. | Corrupt state/event disagreement is rejected; journal reconstruction validates the chain before publishing a new database. |
| P1 | A plan reviewer could approve a major task, then claim the same implementation using their own approval. | Claim evaluates approval with the prospective implementer excluded. | A reviewer cannot claim without a separate eligible plan approval. |
| P1 | An expired lease could transfer implementation to the accepted plan reviewer, bypassing the initial-claim check. | Accepted plan reviewer identities remain recorded and cannot take over that implementation. | Expired takeover is rejected without changing the previous owner. |
| P1 | After handover, a previous implementer could review their own inherited result because only the newest implementer was excluded. | All historical implementation contributors remain excluded from reviews and approval counting. | A separate author, original implementer, successor implementer, and returning contributor reproduce the bypass; the corrected runtime rejects it. |
| P1 | Root implementation scope included generated records; recording a review changed its own approval fingerprint. | Generated projections and session reports are omitted from implementation snapshots. | `--scope .` permits a reviewed claim without self-invalidating its approval. |
| P1 | Scientific analysis evidence was omitted from audit and export. | Run interpretation evidence is checked and transferred alongside output artifacts. | Export contains the analysis; subsequent analysis modification makes audit fail. |
| P1 | Non-UTF-8 generated exports prevented their own repair. | Projection drift detection treats corrupt generated content as rebuildable drift. | `audit --repair` restores corrupt state JSON from the database. |
| P2 | Valid JSON of the wrong shape caused an uncaught exception during integrity checking. | Ledger structure errors produce workflow errors. | Array-shaped state and null-shaped event records are rejected cleanly. |

## Executed validation

Executed locally on Darwin arm64 with Python 3.9.6:

```sh
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_adversarial.py' -v
```

Result: **29 tests passed**, 2.634 seconds. The final run includes the historical-contributor regression added after the initial 28-test run. No Linux, Windows, or hosted CI execution is claimed here.

The suite exercises unacknowledged and stale contexts, maintained-rule changes, forged report hashes, concurrent process sessions and task claims, scoped code and review evidence changes, reviewer independence across handover, corrupt ledger/export refusal, reconstruction with missing state JSON, traversal/symlink rejection, generated-directory write boundaries, timed-out and unavailable commands, durable launcher crash intent, successor recovery, analysis evidence transfer, and successful commands whose changed code invalidates their provenance.

Crash injection raises an unexpected exception at subprocess launch after experiment intent is persisted. It verifies recoverable running state and explicit successor resolution; it does not simulate electrical power loss. Concurrent tests execute distinct processes against one local project.

## Remaining limits

- CLI gates coordinate cooperative agents. Agents can still edit files outside the CLI; recorded scope is not an operating-system sandbox.
- Different reviewer labels and contributor exclusion support traceability. They cannot authenticate a human or prove that separate model processes were independently controlled.
- The hash chain checks local consistency. A party controlling all records can rewrite and rehash history without an external trusted anchor.
- SQLite locking coordinates a local shared checkout. Network filesystems, distributed replicas, and cross-machine lease consensus were not validated.
- Experiments retain command arguments, environment metadata, configuration/data fingerprints, output evidence, and declared code scope. They do not automatically apply the seed, capture every external dependency, preserve unavailable datasets, or establish scientific validity.
- Scope and provenance quality depend on accurately declaring relevant files. Command runtime metadata for alternate interpreters or containers must be supplied by the command itself.

These limits should remain visible in contributor onboarding and release documentation. Additional platform claims require execution on those platforms; production identity or tamper guarantees require separate infrastructure.

documents.AUDIT/phase2-final-report.md:
# UADOS Phase 2 final report

Phase 2 extends the existing dependency-free local UADOS ledger; it does not rebuild its storage or fabricate retrospective governance. Fresh projects use workflow protocol 2. The explicit upgrade retains schema 1, the original event prefix, and protocol-1 interpretation for legacy tasks.

## Architecture

`project.py` owns lifecycle and review gates; `storage.py` owns locking, transactional events, atomic projections and exact-byte evidence archives; `context.py` owns context and Understanding Reports. New `protocol.py`, `orchestration.py` and `governance.py` separate versioning/projections, role/debate control and change/research/improvement records. This keeps provider-independent coordination modular. New adapters specialize file discovery through one maintained master workflow. Extension is possible through declared capabilities, reviewed policies and explicit runtime packets; actual provider dispatch requires an integration. Full-state events favor local traceability but increase storage and verification cost with history.

## Capabilities

Formal startup, task, handover and memory protocols generate and acknowledge Understanding Reports before tracked execution. Every protocol-2 task has an evidence-backed implementation and validation plan. Major work additionally binds seven-field change control, generated role coverage, assignments and three-round analysis/challenge/vote consensus from two eligible independent reviewers. Dissent, rejected alternatives and prior contributors remain visible. Live evidence drift, stale policies and role changes invalidate approval.

Research records preserve truthful literature access and corpus coverage, all seven contribution fields plus coverage limits, provisional independent novelty assessment, a separate falsifiable hypothesis, and exact hypothesis/experiment/run outcomes. Failed execution cannot support a scientific supported/refuted verdict. The scenario reproduces known WLS and records overlap; it makes no scientific novelty claim.

New evidence registration reads bytes once, preserves a verified content-addressed snapshot and records its location. Active gates check both the live source and promised snapshot. Export/Git reconstruction retain archives. Audit reports current consistency separately from historical original-byte availability and fails for a missing or corrupt promised snapshot. Audit findings and investigated fixes appear in the generated improvement log.

## Executed validation

The current suite passed **75 tests** on local macOS arm64/Python 3.9. Independent prior boundary tests and new archive probes inspect ownership, vetoes, selected-role execution, stale research policies, malformed inputs, exact-byte retention, current-path drift, archive corruption and export/rebuild. The three scenarios were rerun under snapshot-aware code in `EXAMPLES/phase2-snapshot-validation`: six application behavior checks, synthetic research with 200 seeded repetitions, and a fresh-process logical Day1/Day30 handover after export/rebuild. The WLS median paired RMSE ratio is 0.7938114563766927 with a conditional bootstrap interval [0.715706307871708, 0.852870340691968].

The rebuilt **1.1.0 wheel includes 48 maintained assets**. Isolated installation, current package-byte equality and a real disposable Git clone reconstruct the root, three historical examples and four Phase2 example projects. `AUDIT/phase2-distribution-v3-final.json`, `AUDIT/phase2-runtime-validation-v3.json`, `AUDIT/phase2-tests-v3.txt` and `AUDIT/phase2-docs-v3.json` retain commands/results. Actual separate model reviewers, distinct from scripted fixture labels, participate in the final plan and result debate; the completed rounds and final state are recorded in `CONSENSUS_DECISION.md` and the final audit, rather than inferred from this report.

## Known limits and integrity findings

Current validation passes, but several earlier Phase2 evidence files were overwritten before archives existed. Historical records remain unchanged and the audit explicitly reports the unavailable original hashes through `history_ok` and `historical_evidence_drift`. These losses cannot be repaired by rehashing replacements; current acceptance uses immutable new revision paths. Phase1 SHA-bound audit/ADR evidence and the original event prefix remain unchanged. Final delivery must be read together with the current audit's historical warnings.

Contributor labels/capabilities cannot authenticate identity or expertise. Adapters supply bootstrap packets; commercial products/providers were not launched. Scripted scenario roles test mechanics, logical dates do not represent 29 elapsed days, and synthetic oracle-weight research does not establish physical validity or publication merit. Hosted Linux/Windows CI, distributed coordination, network-filesystem locks and large-history performance remain unexecuted. Direct editor writes remain outside lease enforcement; the hash chain has no external trust anchor.

## Phase 3

Priorities: authenticated contributor identity and signed audit anchors; provider/native-client dispatch with receipts; protected evidence storage and release artifacts; hosted cross-platform CI; systematic literature access/search integrations; distributed lease coordination; and scalable event storage with performance validation. Domain experiments should add real-data controls, calibration checks and independently reviewed statistical analysis.

documents.AUDIT/phase3-baseline-report.md:
# UADOS Phase 3 Baseline Report

**Inspection date:** 2026-10-13 (Asia/Shanghai)  
**Scope:** read-only architecture, protocol, memory, audit, test and distribution inspection before Phase 3 implementation.  
**Runtime observed:** macOS arm64, Python 3.9.6, dependency-free standard-library runtime.  
**Important record:** starting the required acknowledged UADOS session created the normal `session.start` ledger event S000010; no implementation source or historical evidence was edited during this baseline.

## 1. Current system capability summary

UADOS is a local, provider-neutral R&D workflow framework built around a SQLite authoritative ledger, full-state hash-chained events, generated Markdown/JSON projections, atomic projection writes, stable OS locking, evidence snapshots and rebuildable exports. Fresh projects use protocol 2 while the schema and historical protocol-1 interpretation remain intact.

The current lifecycle is explicit: start and acknowledge an Understanding Report, define scoped work, record implementation and validation plans, obtain risk-proportionate independent review, execute through the CLI, preserve decisions/failures/evidence, run audit, and close with a structured handover. The CLI cannot prove that a contributor read a report, that a declared agent is a distinct person/model, or that a scientific conclusion is valid.

## 2. Implemented functionality

### Core workflow and memory

- SQLite state plus ordered, SHA-256 linked full-state events; current state must equal the last event.
- Stable project lock, immediate transactions, atomic generated projections and projection drift detection/repair.
- Structured session start, Understanding Report hash, acknowledgement, refresh, stale-context gates and generated handovers.
- Task dependencies, explicit scopes, leases, takeover records, contributor history and routine/major completion gates.
- Durable decisions, notes, failed approaches, experiments and exported/rebuilt project records.

### Phase 2 governance and orchestration

- Protocol 2 is additive to schema 1 and preserves Phase 1/legacy event history.
- Seven-field major change requests, implementation/validation plans and generated role plans.
- Capability declarations, explicit role assignments and provider-neutral dispatch packets.
- Three staged debate rounds: analysis, adversarial challenge and vote, followed by consensus binding task/policy/scope/evidence/assignment fingerprints.
- Independent plan/result approval quorum with exclusion of authors and implementation contributors; dissent and rejected alternatives remain historical.
- CLI malformed-input validation, stale-policy invalidation, evidence snapshot creation, current-path checks and historical archive checks.

### Research and audit

- Literature records distinguish full text, abstract and unavailable access; source identifiers and corpus groups are retained.
- Seven-field research ideas, provisional novelty audits, coverage limits and separate falsifiable hypotheses.
- Experiment argument vectors, dataset/configuration manifests, seeds, scoped provenance, timeout/failure/recovery records and exact outcome interpretation.
- Audit separates `ok` from `history_ok`, reports historical evidence drift honestly and checks promised immutable snapshots.
- `audit --record` produces deduplicated proposed improvements; the improvement log does not silently execute fixes.

### Packaging and validation already present

- 48 packaged maintained assets, including hidden `.agent` and Cursor `.mdc` compatibility files.
- Phase 2 acceptance recorded 75 tests, local scenario runs, isolated wheel installation, Git reconstruction and snapshot-aware exports.
- The frozen Phase 2 delivery manifest contains 81 entries and was rechecked in this inspection with zero mismatches.
- The configured CI matrix covers Python 3.9/3.12/3.14 on Ubuntu/macOS/Windows, but hosted runs are not evidence in this local workspace.

## 3. Current state and integrity observations

The ledger currently contains 312 events after the required Phase 3 startup event, 6 completed tasks, 10 sessions, 4 registered agent profiles, 5 role plans, 4 debates, 5 change records and 5 improvement records. There are no literature, idea or hypothesis records in the root project state; research coverage is exercised primarily through fixtures and prior Phase 2 evidence. The local ledger is approximately 338 MB and the JSON state projection approximately 2.6 MB.

The current audit is `ok=true` with no projection or snapshot errors. `history_ok=false` remains correctly reported because four pre-snapshot Phase 2 evidence originals cannot be reconstructed. The 81 frozen Phase 2 files remain byte-identical. This report does not reinterpret those historical limitations as resolved.

The baseline test suite reran successfully: **75 tests in 46.958 seconds**. `scripts/verify_scaffold.py` also passed with 16 required paths, 4 onboarding events in its disposable project and 47 packaged Markdown assets. These are local checks only.

## 4. Missing capabilities

The following gaps are explicit Phase 3 candidates rather than defects hidden by the current audit:

1. **Authenticated identity and signed audit anchors.** Agent IDs, runtime labels and capabilities are cooperative metadata. The local hash chain has no external trust anchor, signature, key rotation or verifier policy.
2. **Provider/native-client dispatch.** Adapters produce context packets but do not invoke Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, Qoder, ZCode or another provider, nor capture a tamper-evident provider receipt.
3. **Protected evidence and release integrity.** Content-addressed snapshots prevent accidental overwrite inside the local project, but access control, encryption, retention, remote object integrity and release attestation are absent.
4. **Hosted cross-platform execution.** The CI matrix is configured but not executed in this environment; Linux, Windows, newer Python, network filesystems and platform-specific lock behavior remain unvalidated.
5. **Distributed coordination and scale.** The stable local lock does not coordinate multiple hosts. Full-state events make history transparent but increase storage and verification costs; the 338 MB local ledger is an early scale signal.
6. **First-class recursive dependency manifests.** Phase 2 manually checked nested evidence for its release. Ordinary evidence registration does not automatically enforce transitive source dependencies after later changes.
7. **Systematic literature integration.** The research registry accepts truthful records, but search/provider adapters, deduplication, retrieval provenance, corpus snapshots and automated coverage reports are not implemented.
8. **Stronger scientific validation.** Fixtures demonstrate bounded mechanics and known-method reproduction; physical data, instrument calibration, non-oracle controls and domain-specific statistical review remain external work.
9. **Release and operations controls.** There is no signed release bundle, migration/version policy beyond the current wheel workflow, metrics/tracing, policy-based retention or recovery drill for remote stores.

## 5. Gap analysis against Phase 3 intent

| Phase 3 intent | Baseline status | Evidence/limit |
|---|---|---|
| Production trust | Partial | Local hash chain, snapshots and audits work; identity and external anchoring absent |
| Intelligent orchestration | Partial | Deterministic roles and debates work; no real provider dispatch or receipt verification |
| Enterprise security | Partial | Path/symlink/input gates exist; no authenticated authorization, encryption or remote policy enforcement |
| Distributed workflow | Local only | SQLite transaction and OS lock are single-project/single-host mechanisms |
| Scalable history | Validated at small scale | Full-state history is transparent; current ledger size warrants benchmark and compaction design |
| Research intelligence | Registry and fixtures | No systematic retrieval/search integration or real-domain scientific validation |
| Portability | Configured, locally tested | Hosted OS/Python matrix remains unexecuted |
| Release confidence | Strong local baseline | Frozen assets, wheel/Git checks and 75 tests pass; no signed release provenance |

## 6. Recommended implementation order

1. **Trust foundation:** introduce a versioned identity/signature and key-verification abstraction, signed audit checkpoints, key rotation/revocation records and explicit verification failures while preserving unsigned legacy history.
2. **Evidence/dependency integrity:** make recursive dependency manifests first-class, atomically snapshot all declared inputs, validate manifests at plan/review/run/audit/export boundaries, and add protected release-bundle verification.
3. **Provider-neutral dispatch receipts:** define an adapter interface and deterministic request/response receipt schema; implement a local fake adapter first, then add real clients only with provider credentials and captured invocation evidence.
4. **Distributed lease and event boundary:** design a pluggable coordination backend with fencing/lease expiry semantics, then benchmark SQLite history and a bounded archive/compaction path without changing the authority contract prematurely.
5. **Hosted validation:** execute the existing CI matrix, lock/rebuild/export probes and scenario suite on supported OS/Python combinations; record unavailable environments separately.
6. **Research integration:** add source-search adapters, corpus manifests, deduplication and retrieval provenance; keep source access and coverage claims explicit and reviewable.
7. **Scientific and operational hardening:** add real-data/control templates, calibration metadata, statistical review hooks, metrics, retention/recovery drills and signed release publication checks.

Each step should be an additive major task with its own plan, change request, independent three-round debate, result review, versioned evidence and final audit. Phase 2 frozen files and the four historical evidence-loss findings must remain unchanged.

## 7. Baseline conclusion

The existing UADOS implementation is a coherent, tested local governance core. Phase 3 should extend trust, evidence integrity, provider integration, distributed coordination, scale and research retrieval through explicit interfaces and reviewed adapters. Replacing the SQLite/event/projection core would discard validated behavior and is outside this baseline recommendation.

# UADOS Phase 2 final report

Phase 2 extends the existing dependency-free local UADOS ledger; it does not rebuild its storage or fabricate retrospective governance. Fresh projects use workflow protocol 2. The explicit upgrade retains schema 1, the original event prefix, and protocol-1 interpretation for legacy tasks.

## Architecture

`project.py` owns lifecycle and review gates; `storage.py` owns locking, transactional events, atomic projections and exact-byte evidence archives; `context.py` owns context and Understanding Reports. New `protocol.py`, `orchestration.py` and `governance.py` separate versioning/projections, role/debate control and change/research/improvement records. This keeps provider-independent coordination modular. New adapters specialize file discovery through one maintained master workflow. Extension is possible through declared capabilities, reviewed policies and explicit runtime packets; actual provider dispatch requires an integration. Full-state events favor local traceability but increase storage and verification cost with history.

## Capabilities

Formal startup, task, handover and memory protocols generate and acknowledge Understanding Reports before tracked execution. Every protocol-2 task has an evidence-backed implementation and validation plan. Major work additionally binds seven-field change control, generated role coverage, assignments and three-round analysis/challenge/vote consensus from two eligible independent reviewers. Dissent, rejected alternatives and prior contributors remain visible. Live evidence drift, stale policies and role changes invalidate approval.

Research records preserve truthful literature access and corpus coverage, all seven contribution fields plus coverage limits, provisional independent novelty assessment, a separate falsifiable hypothesis, and exact hypothesis/experiment/run outcomes. Failed execution cannot support a scientific supported/refuted verdict. The scenario reproduces known WLS and records overlap; it makes no scientific novelty claim.

New evidence registration reads bytes once, preserves a verified content-addressed snapshot and records its location. Active gates check both the live source and promised snapshot. Export/Git reconstruction retain archives. Audit reports current consistency separately from historical original-byte availability and fails for a missing or corrupt promised snapshot. Audit findings and investigated fixes appear in the generated improvement log.

## Executed validation

The current suite passed **75 tests** on local macOS arm64/Python 3.9. Independent prior boundary tests and new archive probes inspect ownership, vetoes, selected-role execution, stale research policies, malformed inputs, exact-byte retention, current-path drift, archive corruption and export/rebuild. The three scenarios were rerun under snapshot-aware code in `EXAMPLES/phase2-snapshot-validation`: six application behavior checks, synthetic research with 200 seeded repetitions, and a fresh-process logical Day1/Day30 handover after export/rebuild. The WLS median paired RMSE ratio is 0.7938114563766927 with a conditional bootstrap interval [0.715706307871708, 0.852870340691968].

The rebuilt **1.1.0 wheel includes 48 maintained assets**. Isolated installation, current package-byte equality and a real disposable Git clone reconstruct the root, three historical examples and four Phase2 example projects. `AUDIT/phase2-distribution-v3-final.json`, `AUDIT/phase2-runtime-validation-v3.json`, `AUDIT/phase2-tests-v3.txt` and `AUDIT/phase2-docs-v3.json` retain commands/results. Actual separate model reviewers, distinct from scripted fixture labels, participate in the final plan and result debate; the completed rounds and final state are recorded in `CONSENSUS_DECISION.md` and the final audit, rather than inferred from this report.

## Known limits and integrity findings

Current validation passes, but several earlier Phase2 evidence files were overwritten before archives existed. Historical records remain unchanged and the audit explicitly reports the unavailable original hashes through `history_ok` and `historical_evidence_drift`. These losses cannot be repaired by rehashing replacements; current acceptance uses immutable new revision paths. Phase1 SHA-bound audit/ADR evidence and the original event prefix remain unchanged. Final delivery must be read together with the current audit's historical warnings.

Contributor labels/capabilities cannot authenticate identity or expertise. Adapters supply bootstrap packets; commercial products/providers were not launched. Scripted scenario roles test mechanics, logical dates do not represent 29 elapsed days, and synthetic oracle-weight research does not establish physical validity or publication merit. Hosted Linux/Windows CI, distributed coordination, network-filesystem locks and large-history performance remain unexecuted. Direct editor writes remain outside lease enforcement; the hash chain has no external trust anchor.

## Phase 3

Priorities: authenticated contributor identity and signed audit anchors; provider/native-client dispatch with receipts; protected evidence storage and release artifacts; hosted cross-platform CI; systematic literature access/search integrations; distributed lease coordination; and scalable event storage with performance validation. Domain experiments should add real-data controls, calibration checks and independently reviewed statistical analysis.

# Phase 2 internal critical review

1. **Is it useful for long-term projects?** Durable decisions, task ownership, hypotheses and evidence snapshots allow recovery after chat loss. Full-state histories and manual provider dispatch limit scale; history performance needs Phase3 measurements.
2. **Can a completely new agent understand it?** A central workflow, formal startup protocol, issued Understanding Report, preserved failures and a structured handover give a file-based entry. The fresh-process export/rebuild scenario reconstructs status, decisions and unfinished work. Acknowledgement cannot prove comprehension or external-resource availability.
3. **Can different agents collaborate?** Declared role selection, leases, dependency gates and actual separate-model analysis/challenge/vote records support cooperative work. Capabilities and labels are declarations; adapters do not launch products or authenticate participants. Scripted fixture labels remain distinguished from actual independent reviewers.
4. **Are decisions traceable?** Hash-chained events retain CR alternatives, individual analyses, objections and ballots, exact H/E/R provenance and rejected proposals. Some early Phase2 evidence paths were overwritten before snapshots, so original hashes are reported as historical loss; traceability must not be confused with preserved original bytes or authenticity.
5. **Is it an enterprise system or only documentation?** It has executable state transitions, stale-input rejection, ownership/independence gates, three debate rounds, change control, research records, audit diagnostics, raw experiment execution and recovery. It remains a local framework requiring external identity, provider dispatch, deployment and distributed operations for enterprise use.
6. **What weaknesses remain?** Local trust, editor writes outside leases, no external hash anchor, increasing event-history cost, manual capabilities and source access, bounded novelty assessment, synthetic research and unexecuted hosted-platform/provider checks. Current consistency and historical integrity have separate audit fields; warnings are disclosed rather than hidden.

Meaningful mistake and correction: rerunning validation into already referenced filenames destroyed earlier evidence bytes. Independent review reproduced the failed clone audit. Fresh result paths and exact-byte archives now preserve future originals; active gates continue to reject edited live files. Missing pre-archive originals are explicitly retained as unresolved historical integrity findings. No participant votes or unavailable execution results were fabricated during provider403/429 interruptions.
