# Agent client compatibility

UADOS provides a common project record and lifecycle through [MASTER_AGENT_WORKFLOW.md](../MASTER_AGENT_WORKFLOW.md). Its native entry files request explicit reading of that authority; this is a compatibility contract, not proof that a product obeyed it. No provider credentials, hidden API calls or commercial client launch are required by the local CLI.

Official loader documentation was checked on **2026-10-12**. Loader behavior can change; recheck product documentation when upgrading.

| Client | UADOS entry | Documented discovery and relevant limit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Codex | Root `AGENTS.md` | Loads instructions from root toward working directory; `AGENTS.override.md` and configured fallbacks can take precedence. Combined project instructions default to a 32 KiB limit. Keep this adapter short and explicitly read the master. [Official documentation](https://developers.openai.com/codex/guides/agents-md) |
| Claude Code | Root `CLAUDE.md` importing `@MASTER_AGENT_WORKFLOW.md` | Markdown imports are supported. Native `AGENTS.md` discovery is version/settings dependent; the supplied CLAUDE entry avoids relying on it. If import is unavailable, read the master explicitly. [Official documentation](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory) |
| Cursor | `.cursor/rules/uados.mdc` | Project rules use `.mdc` with frontmatter; plain `.md` in this directory is ignored. `alwaysApply: true` activates the wrapper. Referenced files are not automatically inlined, so its body instructs an explicit read. Root `AGENTS.md` is also supported. [Official documentation](https://cursor.com/docs/rules) |
| Qoder | Root `AGENTS.md` | Automatically recognizes AGENTS. Native `.qoder/rules` take precedence on conflicts; active rule content has a combined size limit. The entry uses a plain file path and explicit read instruction, not an assumed import. [Official documentation](https://docs.qoder.com/user-guide/rules) |
| ZCode | Root `AGENTS.md` | Documents global and workspace AGENTS sources. CLAUDE migration is onboarding behavior, not continuous runtime loading. This contract does not assume nested discovery, imports or a shared merge algorithm. [Official documentation](https://zcode.z.ai/en/docs/agents) |

Adapters do not duplicate lifecycle rules. `.cursor/rules/uados.md` remains a portable human reference alongside the actual `.mdc` wrapper. Native product instructions may change precedence; inspect them without silently overwriting existing files during adoption.

Role selection produces provider-neutral assignments and a dispatch packet with task/context/instructions. A human or authorized host starts actual independent contributors and supplies their results through the CLI. Capability labels and agent labels are declared metadata, not verified model skills or identity. The team must establish actual independence.

Local validation covers maintained file parity, packaged hidden/nested assets, CLI behavior and simulated identity switching. It does not claim end-to-end execution of Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, Qoder and ZCode. Commercial-client integration, provider dispatch, native hooks, remote authentication and client-specific automated enforcement remain explicit integrations to test.

# Agent handover protocol

Authority: [master workflow, section 6](../MASTER_AGENT_WORKFLOW.md#6-close-with-a-usable-handover). `SESSION_HANDOVER.md` is generated by session closure; this worksheet is preparation material, not an alternative register.

Before closing, assemble current status, completed work with validation, remaining task IDs, known problems, important decision IDs, rejected approaches and recommended next actions. Include paths, exact commands and access/environment constraints needed by a contributor who cannot read the old chat. Distinguish done, submitted for review, blocked and unvalidated work.

Use `session close` with the concise summary and actionable next steps; include actual blockers and failed approaches. Check generated handover and audit. Preserve unfinished implementation artifacts and contributor history. The incoming agent checks the ledger, task leases, evidence fingerprints and resource availability, starts its own stable session and uses the master's context procedure.

A scenario labeled “Day 1 Claude Code → Day 30 Codex” may use logical day labels to test recovery. Such labels do not establish 30 elapsed days or actual commercial-client invocation. Report the simulation method and invocation evidence separately.

# Project memory update protocol

Authority: [master workflow, section 3](../MASTER_AGENT_WORKFLOW.md#3-execute-and-preserve-reasoning). See [PROJECT_MEMORY/README.md](../PROJECT_MEMORY/README.md) for the resource map.

Route a fact to one primary record: task outcome and evidence through task commands; significant choices through decision/change records; experiment execution and interpretation through research commands; technical explanations, lessons and failures through `note` or maintained `PROJECT_MEMORY/notes/`; stopping context through session closure. Keep architecture and policies maintained, with a tracked rationale for significant changes.

A durable note names its task/source, observation date or event, scope, conclusion, evidence strength, uncertainty and affected next decision. Preserve negative results, rejected alternatives and failure triggers. Record resource identifiers and authorized retrieval instructions without credentials or confidential raw data.

Generated views are read-only inputs for contributors. Repair projection drift from the ledger using the master's audit procedure; do not edit the view to make evidence appear consistent. After changing governed maintained memory, refresh affected sessions and inspect the new context report. A content hash supports comparison of bytes; it is not proof of honest observation.

# Agent startup protocol

Authority: [master workflow, section 1](../MASTER_AGENT_WORKFLOW.md#1-establish-context-before-action). This operational worksheet supports startup without replacing its gates.

Prepare a context packet with stable contributor label, client/runtime name if known, project root, recorded mode, intended task, policy version and current resource access. Inspect mode-detection evidence; distinguish a classification assumption from an observed resource. Read the task and dependencies before proposing parallel work.

The issued `PROJECT UNDERSTANDING REPORT` is the startup output. Verify its objective, phase, architecture, completed work, problems, risks, resource inventory and next actions against their files. Add explicit findings for missing data, unavailable services, resource constraints and unresolved assumptions. Do not fabricate capability or availability from a filename.

Record the exact issued report hash, acknowledge it and prepare the evidence-backed execution plan required for the task's protocol. Keep the report in the generated session register. If tracked state or governed documents change, use the master's refresh/acknowledgement procedure. Read [compatibility.md](compatibility.md) when the client cannot discover these instructions reliably.

# Task execution protocol

Authority: [master workflow, sections 2–4](../MASTER_AGENT_WORKFLOW.md#2-define-and-review-owned-work). Use this worksheet to assemble the task packet; the task's recorded protocol controls its gates.

| Stage | Concrete record or outcome |
| --- | --- |
| Task definition | Observable outcome, acceptance criteria, scopes, dependencies and existing-work inspection |
| Risk assessment | Consequence of failure and why routine/major classification fits |
| Implementation plan | Proposed steps, alternatives, recovery and meaningful validation; readable supporting evidence |
| Multi-agent review | Independent challenge; protocol-2 major role coverage, debate rounds and consensus |
| Execution | Claimed ownership and coherent maintained implementation |
| Validation | Executed commands/procedures, inputs, environment, failures and result evidence |
| Documentation update | Architecture, rationale, lessons and acceptance gaps in their proper maintained/ledger records |
| Final audit | Current consistency result and unresolved findings; current major result approvals before completion |

Review changes with the [debate protocol](../MULTI_AGENT_SYSTEM/debate_protocol.md) and [change policy](../CHANGE_REQUESTS/CHANGE_POLICY.md). A new task plan is a durable record, not a chat-only promise. Keep validation evidence outside generated files and preserve original failures. When a resource or ownership conflict blocks work, record the actual issue and a specific recovery action rather than lowering risk or inventing success.

# UADOS Cursor reference

This Markdown file is a portable reference for people and adapters. Cursor project-rule loading uses `.mdc`; the active wrapper is `uados.mdc` in this directory.

Read `MASTER_AGENT_WORKFLOW.md` from the project root before work and follow that central lifecycle. Open its applicable `.agent/` protocols, memory and policies explicitly. See `.agent/compatibility.md` for discovery limits.

---
description: UADOS project lifecycle entry
alwaysApply: true
---

Before editing implementation or running a substantive experiment, explicitly open `MASTER_AGENT_WORKFLOW.md` from the project root and follow its recorded lifecycle. Open the applicable `.agent/` protocols referenced there. This instruction is always applied; referenced files are not assumed to be inlined. The master workflow is the single UADOS lifecycle authority. Client discovery details are in `.agent/compatibility.md`.

# UADOS agent entry

Before editing implementation or running a substantive experiment, read `MASTER_AGENT_WORKFLOW.md` from the project root and follow its recorded lifecycle. It is the single authority for UADOS startup, task ownership, review, validation, memory updates and handover.

Then read the applicable `.agent/` protocols referenced by that workflow, project memory, task dependencies and engineering or research policies. If this client does not load referenced files automatically, open them explicitly. A file reference does not establish that its contents were read.

Use a stable contributor identity, inspect and acknowledge the exact issued Understanding Report, and work through the project's CLI. Native product instructions and project-specific rules may affect discovery; inspect `.agent/compatibility.md` when configuring an agent client.

# Audit and recovery

The ledger is authoritative; generated files are readable projections. Audit checks consistency of the stored record and recorded evidence. It cannot establish that a scientific claim is correct or that a collaborator is authentic.

```sh
python -m uados --project . audit
python -m uados --project . audit --repair
```

Use the command's result and diagnostics as the record of what was inspected. `--repair` regenerates projections from a valid ledger. It does not rewrite history, invent missing evidence or restore altered scoped files.

## Recovery decisions

| Observation | Interpretation | Response |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Generated Markdown or JSON differs | Projection drift or interrupted generation | Preserve useful diagnostics, then repair projections and audit again |
| Evidence is missing or changed | The recorded claim cannot be verified against its original artifact | Restore the exact artifact from a trusted backup or rerun validation and record new evidence; obtain a fresh review when needed |
| Ledger hash chain or state is inconsistent | Authoritative-record integrity is uncertain | Stop tracked work, preserve a copy and restore a verified backup; do not “fix” the chain by hand |
| Session context is stale | Recorded state or maintained context changed | Refresh, inspect the new report and acknowledge its hash |
| Conflicting active ownership | Parallel work overlaps or an earlier owner left | Coordinate takeover and record the reason; do not remove a lock or overwrite files blindly |
| Experiment was interrupted | Execution may have partial outputs or a surviving process | Inspect execution state, stop it through an appropriate authorized mechanism if needed, then use `experiment resolve` with the recovery reason before a safe rerun |
| Required resource is unavailable | Validation cannot establish the intended claim | Record a blocker and recovery action; do not call the result empty or passing |

## Locking and interrupted writes

The CLI holds a stable operating-system project lock across record mutation and projection generation. Process exit releases the operating-system lock; the lock file may remain and is not itself evidence that a process still owns it. Do not unlink a lock file to bypass a competing writer, because separate writers could then lock different inodes.

SQLite commits ledger event and current state together. Projection files are generated after that commit and can be rebuilt if generation stops. An interrupted projection write therefore needs regeneration, while a failed database commit needs investigation of the record before further work. If the CLI reports that an event committed but projection generation failed, do not repeat the original action: repair and inspect the committed state first.

## Preservation and restart

Keep a verified backup of ledger, maintained documents and relevant evidence. Before destructive recovery, retain the original files and diagnostics. After restoring, audit, inspect the latest handover and start a new acknowledged session. Revalidate external resources; a copied project does not establish their current availability.

If the local database is absent after a Git clone, `rebuild-ledger` can reconstruct it from a complete validated `.uados/events.jsonl` and matching exported state when present. Preserve a consistent Git revision of memory and evidence as well. The command refuses an existing database; it is not a corruption-overwrite mechanism. If exports disagree, recover a coherent revision instead of editing hashes until validation passes.

When an audit reveals a repeated failure, record a lesson and review a bounded policy improvement using `ENGINEERING_RULES/extensions.md`.

# Enterprise change policy

Lifecycle authority: [MASTER_AGENT_WORKFLOW.md](../MASTER_AGENT_WORKFLOW.md). For protocol-2 major modifications, use a structured change request linked to the task before its plan review. This gives the design-document/RFC/ADR process a durable record without replacing task ownership or acceptance gates.

Required fields are **Problem, Background, Alternatives, Decision, Impact, Risk and Validation**. Alternatives need at least two entries; evidence must be readable and relevant. Use [CR_TEMPLATE.md](CR_TEMPLATE.md) to prepare the content. Include compatibility, persistent-format impact, resource/authority constraints and recovery when relevant.

The recorded decision is proposed work until the task's governed review and completion establish its disposition. Generate roles, obtain independent analysis and adversarial challenges, and record consensus/plan approval before claim. After implementation, validate and conduct result debate/review over current contents. A material change to scope, assumptions, request or evidence requires renewed planning/review.

`CHANGE_REQUESTS/CR*.md` is generated from the ledger; the maintained template is the exception. Preserve rejected alternatives and superseded records. Use `decision add` for related architectural rationale when its separate fields aid long-term recovery; refer to the same evidence rather than duplicating mutable status.

Legacy protocol-1 tasks keep their recorded lifecycle. Enabling protocol 2 is explicit and preserves old events/tasks; do not retroactively invent change requests for historical approvals. Normal audit can propose improvements but never authorizes an automatic implementation or external deployment.

# Major change request worksheet

Use this maintained worksheet to prepare the structured change-request operation. Generated `CR*.md` records come from the ledger; do not copy this worksheet into a manually approved record. See [CHANGE_POLICY.md](CHANGE_POLICY.md).

## Problem

Concrete trigger, observed behavior and affected users or research claims:

## Background

Current architecture, prior decisions, dependencies and relevant evidence:

## Alternatives

Describe at least two viable choices, including keeping the current behavior when meaningful. Compare costs, compatibility, validity and recovery:

## Decision

Proposed selected choice and why the available evidence favors it:

## Impact

Affected interfaces, persistent records, contributors, resources and migration/rollback:

## Risk

Failure modes, unsupported assumptions, authority/access constraints and accepted uncertainty:

## Validation

Falsifiable acceptance checks, exact procedures/commands, inputs/environment, expected outcomes and required evidence:

Link the task and readable evidence. Do not include credentials or confidential raw material.


## JSON submission shape

Replace every placeholder and create the referenced evidence before submission. Use `change propose TASK_ID --record evidence/change.json --session SESSION_ID`; the JSON file is maintained input, while the resulting `CR000001.md`-style record is generated.

```json
{
  "problem": "Observed trigger and impact",
  "background": "Current architecture and prior evidence",
  "alternatives": ["Preserve current behavior with stated cost", "Proposed bounded change with stated trade-off"],
  "decision": "Selected approach and rationale",
  "impact": "Affected interfaces, resources and migration",
  "risk": "Failure modes, uncertainties and recovery",
  "validation": "Falsifiable checks and expected outcomes",
  "evidence": ["evidence/change-design.md"]
}
```

# Engineering rules

These are maintained team policies. They turn a project's risks into reviewable work rather than replacing judgment with a universal checklist.

- `software.md`: architecture, interfaces, dependencies and operational behavior.
- `quality.md`: risk classification, evidence and completion criteria.
- `security.md`: trust boundaries, secrets, data and executable research commands.
- `extensions.md`: introducing or changing project-specific rules.

Read the rules relevant to the task before acknowledging context. Apply software rules in software and hybrid modes. Apply research rules in research and hybrid modes; research code still needs appropriate software quality and security review.

The CLI implements a finite set of gates: acknowledged context, task ownership/dependencies, evidence requirements and independent plan/result approvals. Protocol-2 tasks add evidence-backed plans; major work adds change requests, role coverage and staged debate/consensus. The single lifecycle authority is `MASTER_AGENT_WORKFLOW.md`; `MULTI_AGENT_SYSTEM/` and `CHANGE_REQUESTS/` explain the specialized records. It does not automatically enforce every policy statement or configure CI, identity providers, Git hosting, provider dispatch or deployment.

If rules conflict, follow applicable law and organizational constraints, then explicit project authorization, then the project's approved policies. Record a policy conflict and its resolution before consequential work. Exceptions need a named reason, bounded scope, owner and expiry or revisit condition; do not silently weaken a rule.

# Rule extension and continuous improvement

Extensions are maintained project policies, not arbitrary executable plugins. They let a project specialize the common workflow without hiding expectations in a conversation.

## Propose a bounded change

Use `TEMPLATES/extension.md` to identify the observed problem, evidence, proposed rule, affected roles, cost, enforcement mechanism and success measure. Link the failure or lesson that motivated it. State whether the rule is a contributor obligation, a CI check, or requires a future CLI implementation; prose alone does not create an automated gate.

Record a decision with alternatives, including retaining the present policy. Changes to lifecycle gates, risk classification, research validity or authority boundaries should be major tasks with independent plan and result review.

## Install the policy

Put approved rules in the appropriate maintained document and add a clear link from its directory README. Include owner, applicability, version or decision reference and revisit condition. Prefer a focused rule over a second conflicting workflow. Include a migration action for existing tasks when necessary.

Maintained policies are context inputs. Their modification invalidates an older session's context where applicable. After the change, refresh affected sessions, read the new Understanding Report and acknowledge its new hash before further tracked work. A contributor must not keep using an older acknowledgement to bypass a newly approved rule.

## Evaluate and revise

Assess whether the rule prevented the original problem and whether it added unreasonable effort or false alarms. Record evidence and exceptions. To retire or revise it, record the reason and review the change at the appropriate risk level. Preserve the historical decision and lessons; do not erase why the team adopted the rule.

Examples of useful extensions include a data leakage check for a particular experiment family, an API compatibility check, an approved instrument calibration protocol or a required migration dry run. External CI and integrations remain explicit team-owned configuration.

# Quality and evidence policy

## Risk classification

Use `routine` for bounded changes with well-understood failure modes. Use `major` for architectural changes, public compatibility changes, security or privacy boundaries, persistent-state integrity, costly experiments, consequential scientific claims or other decisions with substantial impact. When uncertain, describe the uncertainty and select review depth proportionate to potential harm.

The task's recorded protocol controls review gates under `MASTER_AGENT_WORKFLOW.md`. Major tasks require independent plan approval before claim and independent result approval before completion. Protocol-2 major work additionally needs a change request, generated role coverage and staged plan/result consensus with at least two independent reviewers. Reviewers must be different contributors in practice as well as have different recorded labels; task authors and current/past implementers cannot provide independent approval. A change in task, scope, policy, evidence, result, assignments or capabilities can invalidate the relevant review/consensus.

## Evidence requirements

Evidence should answer the claim. A passing command is insufficient when it tests the wrong property. Record:

- The relevant acceptance criterion or hypothesis.
- Exact commands or procedures, inputs and environment.
- Exit status and material output, including failures.
- Expected and observed behavior, uncertainty and uncovered limitations.
- A durable artifact path and the task, decision or experiment it supports.

Use targeted regression checks for behavior changes, boundary and failure checks for integrity-sensitive code, and suitable experimental analysis for research. Routine documentation edits usually need link/consistency review rather than artificial unit tests. Follow additional checks required by the project's toolchain.

Evidence fingerprints reveal a difference from recorded bytes. They cannot establish that an output was honestly produced or that a conclusion follows from it. Review the substance.

## Definition of done

A task is ready to complete when the intended behavior exists, the acceptance criteria are assessed, meaningful validation evidence is recorded, relevant documentation and decisions are updated, and material limitations have owners or explicit disposition. Major work additionally needs an approved result covering the current task, scoped files and evidence.

Do not mark a task complete merely because the implementation compiles, an experiment exits successfully, or a chat message asserts success. If criteria remain unmet, record a blocker or follow-up with a concrete next action.

## Defects and lessons

For a defect, preserve a reproducible trigger and observed impact. Record the failed assumption, fix and verification. Generalize a repeated issue into a reviewed policy extension only when the new rule has a clear benefit and bounded cost. Keep the original evidence so the rule can later be evaluated.


Record validation results to a new, versioned artifact path. Never overwrite a file after a task, review, change, experiment or debate has referenced its bytes; record a new result and obtain the required current review. UADOS archives exact registered bytes, but current-path drift still invalidates active approvals. Audit distinguishes current consistency from historical original-byte availability; inspect both `ok` and `history_ok`, and preserve reported historical loss honestly.

# Security and trust boundaries

## Local trust model

UADOS is a local coordination and provenance tool for trusted collaborators. Anyone with write access to the project can modify implementation, evidence and the SQLite ledger. A hash chain detects accidental inconsistency and unsynchronized edits under the tool's model; it is not a signature, an authenticated audit service or a defense against a writer who rewrites the record.

Agent IDs are team-chosen labels. Distinct IDs support ownership and review checks, but cannot prove a distinct person or model performed the review. Use organizational identity, protected storage or external review systems if stronger guarantees are required.

Task scope and leases coordinate work; they do not restrict editor or operating-system access. Tracked-command acknowledgement cannot prove a contributor read the report. Hold contributors responsible for these policies.

## Secrets and sensitive data

Never commit tokens, passwords, private keys or access credentials to notes, evidence, commands, configuration snapshots or handovers. Use the project's approved credential mechanism. Record only the name of the required secret and how an authorized contributor obtains it.

Minimize sensitive data in logs and manifests. Record access restrictions and de-identification needs. A reproducibility goal does not authorize sharing personal, proprietary or restricted data. Inspect an export or release for accidental disclosure before sharing it.

## Executable inputs

Treat code, downloaded files, dataset processing scripts and command arguments as executable trust decisions. `experiment run` executes the recorded argument vector with the user's privileges. It is not a sandbox. Read the command and relevant program before execution; bound runtime and resources where feasible. Avoid destructive commands or shell wrappers unless explicitly necessary and authorized.

Fingerprinting a file does not make its contents safe. Validate format and size assumptions at ingestion, and record source and license before incorporating external material.

## Review triggers and response

Use major review for authentication, authorization, exposed interfaces, handling of sensitive data and persistent-record integrity. Examine concrete failure paths, least privilege, input validation, dependency provenance and recovery.

When a security issue is found, preserve a minimal sanitized reproducer, document impact and uncertainty, assign ownership and avoid distributing exploit details beyond the authorized audience. If credentials were exposed, use the organization's rotation process; editing the visible file does not remove all historical copies.

# Software engineering policy

## Design and implementation

Give each component a clear responsibility and explicit interfaces. Prefer a simple design that meets current requirements and leaves known extension points. Record major architectural choices with a problem, alternatives, evidence, rationale and limitations.

Before changing a public interface or persistent format, identify callers, compatibility requirements, migration and rollback. Treat silent data loss, incompatible contracts and altered security boundaries as major risk. Put behavioral and acceptance criteria in the task rather than leaving them only in implementation comments.

Keep edits within agreed ownership and scope. Separate unrelated changes when doing so improves review and recovery. Document important invariants, failure paths and non-obvious reasoning near the implementation or in memory.

## Dependencies and environment

Document supported runtimes and installation commands. Prefer existing dependencies when they serve the purpose. Before adding one, examine its license, maintenance, attack surface, transitive cost and reproducibility needs. Record version selection and meaningful upgrade changes. A dependency name without a resolvable version or lock strategy is inadequate for a claimed reproducible environment.

Do not introduce hidden network, shell, account or service requirements. If a feature needs them, state them in the plan and validate failure behavior when unavailable.

## Reliability and performance

Make errors actionable and preserve enough context to diagnose them without secrets. Distinguish retryable failure, invalid input and corrupted state. Bound long-running work with cancellation or timeouts when the interface permits them. Avoid reporting success before outputs are actually durable.

Measure performance against an explicit workload and budget. Record hardware, environment, repetitions and variability. Do not claim a universal speedup from one favorable run. Address correctness and operability alongside throughput.

## Delivery

Before release, verify acceptance criteria, relevant automated checks, supported environments, documentation and migration/recovery. Record the tested revision and evidence. CI, packaging, protected branches and deployments are optional integrations that must be configured and verified by the team; UADOS does not deploy them automatically.

See `VERSION_CONTROL/README.md` for ownership, review and release evidence practices.

# Worked workflows

These walkthroughs use the actual CLI, with IDs/hashes copied from its JSON output. Replace uppercase placeholders. They describe a local trusted-team workflow; starting an independent reviewer is the responsibility of your agent environment or team.

## Routine software work and agent handover

Initialize a new directory after installing UADOS:

```sh
python -m uados init ./example-app --name "Example app" \
  --objective "Build and validate a small service" --mode software
python -m uados --project ./example-app session start --agent implementer-A
python -m uados --project ./example-app session acknowledge SESSION_A \
  --report-hash REPORT_HASH_A
python -m uados --project ./example-app task add --session SESSION_A \
  --title "Validate input boundaries" \
  --description "Reject malformed inputs and preserve valid input behavior; verify both" \
  --risk routine --scope src/validator.py
python -m uados --project ./example-app task claim TASK_ID --session SESSION_A
```

Create the implementation and run the relevant checks. Save actual results at `example-app/evidence/validation.txt`; do not use fabricated passing output. Then record and complete:

```sh
python -m uados --project ./example-app task record TASK_ID --session SESSION_A \
  --summary "Implemented input boundaries; valid and malformed cases checked" \
  --evidence evidence/validation.txt
python -m uados --project ./example-app task complete TASK_ID --session SESSION_A
python -m uados --project ./example-app session close SESSION_A \
  --summary "Boundary validation completed with recorded checks" \
  --next "Review the validator task evidence and define the next service behavior"
python -m uados --project ./example-app session start --agent implementer-B
```

Agent B reads the new report and source documents, acknowledges its hash and continues. Completed work, evidence and next action come from the project record rather than Agent A's chat. If maintained context was edited between commands, refresh and acknowledge before proceeding.

## Major change with independent review

Create a major task with explicit scope and a plan artifact. A genuinely separate reviewer starts and acknowledges a session, challenges the plan and records:

```sh
python -m uados --project . task review TASK_ID --session REVIEW_SESSION \
  --stage plan --verdict approve \
  --challenge "Examined migration failure paths; staged writes preserve existing records" \
  --evidence evidence/plan-review.md
```

The implementer refreshes and acknowledges because the review changed project context, then claims the task. After implementation, validation and `task record`, the reviewer refreshes and acknowledges, inspects the actual result and records a result review. The implementer refreshes and acknowledges again before completion.

The challenge text above is an example of form, not proof that a migration was tested. Each team's review must refer to its actual artifacts.

| Attempt | Expected behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Claim a major task without a current independent plan approval | Rejected |
| Review under the task author/implementer's agent label | Rejected |
| Complete without submitted evidence | Rejected |
| Complete major work without a current approved result | Rejected |
| Change scoped implementation after submission/review | Record and review the changed result again |
| Act with stale maintained or recorded context | Refresh, inspect and acknowledge again |

## Research result and negative finding

Put an experiment script, JSON configuration and input manifest in the project. Define the hypothesis and analysis protocol first, then register:

```sh
python -m uados --project . experiment add --session RESEARCH_SESSION \
  --title "Compare a candidate with a baseline" \
  --hypothesis "The prespecified metric improves over the baseline" \
  --command-json '["python3", "experiment.py", "--config", "config.json"]' \
  --config config.json --dataset data/manifest.json --seed 7 \
  --scope experiment.py --cwd .
python -m uados --project . experiment run EXPERIMENT_ID \
  --session RESEARCH_SESSION --timeout 300
```

The process result records operational success or failure and output paths. Refresh and acknowledge the session, analyze the observations in `evidence/analysis.md`, and conclude:

```sh
python -m uados --project . experiment conclude EXPERIMENT_ID \
  --session RESEARCH_SESSION \
  --conclusion "The candidate did not improve the metric in the measured setting; further datasets remain untested" \
  --evidence evidence/analysis.md
```

A valid negative finding stays in the project memory. If the launcher vanished and the ledger still says running, inspect process state and use `experiment resolve` with a recovery reason after execution has stopped. Preserve a separate record for the rerun.

## Drift and recovery

Run `audit`. If only generated projections differ, inspect diagnostics and run `audit --repair`; then audit again. Changed evidence remains an error requiring restored evidence or new validation, not projection repair. A corrupt ledger requires preservation and verified backup recovery.

For a portable copy, use `export` to a new directory outside the project and explicitly include additional dependencies omitted from recorded scopes. Inspect the copy for private data and run its audit before relying on it. External services, restricted data and installed environments must be restored separately.

# Master agent workflow

This is the single UADOS lifecycle authority. Product entry files point here; `.agent/` files supply operational guidance, and engineering, research and multi-agent policies specialize evidence and review. Project records must let a contributor resume without the previous chat. CLI gates support this contract but cannot prove comprehension, identity or scientific truth.

## 1. Establish context before action

Read in this order:

1. This workflow and the applicable native agent entry file.
2. `PROJECT_STATE.md` and `SESSION_HANDOVER.md`.
3. `PROJECT_MEMORY/README.md`, architecture, current task, dependencies and relevant notes.
4. `DEVELOPMENT_LOG.md` and `DECISION_RECORD.md` for the planned area.
5. Relevant `ENGINEERING_RULES/`, `RESEARCH_MANAGEMENT/`, `MULTI_AGENT_SYSTEM/` and `CHANGE_REQUESTS/` policies.
6. Scoped implementation, data and evidence underlying the claims; summaries alone are insufficient.

Use the startup guidance in [.agent/startup_protocol.md](.agent/startup_protocol.md). Identify yourself with a stable team label; determine software, research or hybrid mode from recorded detection and actual project resources. Explicitly state missing resources and unresolved assumptions. Inspect existing tasks before creating overlapping work.

```sh
python -m uados --project . session start --agent AGENT_ID
```

Inspect the issued **PROJECT UNDERSTANDING REPORT** and its underlying source files. Check objective, phase, architecture, completed work, problems, risks, resources, decisions, failures and recommended next actions. An inventory of files is not a check that data, hardware or external services are available. Prepare an execution plan before implementation.

```sh
python -m uados --project . session acknowledge SESSION_ID --report-hash REPORT_HASH
```

Acknowledgement must use the exact report hash you inspected. Tracked work requires current acknowledgement. When context changes, run `session refresh SESSION_ID`, inspect the replacement report and acknowledge its new hash. Other recorded work and maintained policy changes can make context stale. Do not bypass a stale-context error with a different label.

## 2. Define and review owned work

Follow [.agent/task_execution_protocol.md](.agent/task_execution_protocol.md): task definition → risk assessment → implementation plan → review → execution → validation → documentation → final audit.

```sh
python -m uados --project . task add --session SESSION_ID \
  --title "Describe the observable outcome" \
  --description "Problem and acceptance criteria" \
  --risk routine --scope src/component
```

Repeat `--scope PATH` and `--depends TASK_ID` as needed. Select `major` for architecture, public behavior, persistent integrity, security/data boundaries, research validity, material cost or other consequential changes. Do not split a major decision into nominally routine tasks to evade review.

Fresh projects use workflow protocol 2. Every protocol-2 task needs a recorded implementation plan, validation plan and evidence before claim. A major task additionally needs a seven-field change request with at least two alternatives, generated roles and completed evidence-bound plan debate/consensus plus independent plan approval. See [change policy](CHANGE_REQUESTS/CHANGE_POLICY.md) and [multi-agent policy](MULTI_AGENT_SYSTEM/README.md). Record the plan using the task ID printed by `task add` and existing readable evidence:

```sh
python -m uados --project . task plan TASK_ID --session SESSION_ID \
  --implementation "Steps, assumptions, alternatives and recovery" \
  --validation "Checks, inputs and expected outcomes" \
  --evidence evidence/plan.md
```

For protocol-2 major work, prepare a project-relative JSON change record using `CHANGE_REQUESTS/CR_TEMPLATE.md`, then use `change propose TASK_ID --record evidence/change.json --session SESSION_ID`. Register contributors with `agent register --capability CAPABILITY --session SESSION_ID`, generate roles with `roles generate TASK_ID --session SESSION_ID`, inspect candidates with `roles select ROLE_PLAN_ID` and explicitly assign them with `roles assign ROLE_PLAN_ID --role ROLE_ID --agent AGENT_ID --session SESSION_ID`. Use the IDs printed by the CLI; examples are placeholders, not existing project records.

Open the plan debate with `debate open TASK_ID --roles ROLE_PLAN_ID --stage plan --session SESSION_ID`. Each contributor obtains a read-only packet with `debate packet DEBATE_ID --agent AGENT_ID`, submits analysis and challenges, votes and records consensus using the exact forms in `MULTI_AGENT_SYSTEM/debate_protocol.md`. Consensus records eligible independent approvals from reviewer votes. `task review` remains available for an additional challenged approval; a standalone report or approval does not satisfy the required debate. Use each operation's `--help` for all required fields.

Legacy protocol-1 tasks retain their recorded gates: an independent challenged plan approval before major claim and an independent challenged result approval before major completion. An explicit `upgrade --session SESSION_ID --task OWNED_LEGACY_MAJOR_TASK_ID` enables protocol 2 for newly created tasks; it does not reinterpret historical tasks or replace ledger history. Never treat a legacy approval as protocol-2 consensus.

Reviewers must independently inspect assumptions, relevant files and evidence. A protocol-2 major debate needs at least two independent reviewers, each outside task author and current/past implementation contributors. Distinct labels alone do not establish independent people or models. Assign coverage using declared capabilities and record who actually performs each role.

Claim the task in the implementing session only after required planning, dependencies and approvals are satisfied. Active leases reject overlapping declared scopes, including ancestor/descendant paths. Paths describe ownership and review scope, not an OS sandbox. Do not overwrite active work. Coordinate outside-scope changes, revise scope/plan as appropriate, or record a blocker and a recovery action when ownership, authority or resources prevent progress.

## 3. Execute and preserve reasoning

Make the smallest coherent change satisfying the approved task. Keep implementation, documentation and meaningful validation together. Editor operations are not automatically logged; record important findings through the CLI.

Use `decision add` for durable rationale: problem, alternatives, decision, reason, evidence and risk. Use `note` for technical explanations, lessons, failures or research observations. Preserve rejected approaches with their trigger, command, inputs and observed result. If scope or assumptions change materially, revise the plan and obtain renewed review before dependent execution.

Edit maintained files. Never hand-edit generated `PROJECT_STATE.md`, `DEVELOPMENT_LOG.md`, `DECISION_RECORD.md`, `SESSION_HANDOVER.md`, `CONSENSUS_DECISION.md`, `SYSTEM_IMPROVEMENT_LOG.md`, `PROJECT_MEMORY/tasks.md`, `PROJECT_MEMORY/knowledge.md`, `PROJECT_MEMORY/session_reports/`, `MULTI_AGENT_SYSTEM/role_plans.md`, `CHANGE_REQUESTS/CR*.md` records (except the maintained `CR_TEMPLATE.md`), `RESEARCH_MANAGEMENT/experiments.md`, `RESEARCH_MANAGEMENT/NOVELTY_AUDIT.md`, `RESEARCH_MANAGEMENT/LITERATURE_GAP_ANALYSIS.md`, `RESEARCH_MANAGEMENT/RESEARCH_DECISION_RECORD.md`, `RESEARCH_MANAGEMENT/HYPOTHESES.md`, `.uados/state.json` or `.uados/events.jsonl`. Record free-form durable knowledge under `PROJECT_MEMORY/notes/` or with `note`; follow [.agent/memory_update_protocol.md](.agent/memory_update_protocol.md).

## 4. Validate and challenge the result

Run checks proportionate to risk. Evidence must include the exact command or procedure, relevant inputs/environment, exit status, material results, failures and limits. Do not describe unexecuted checks as passing or unavailable sources as empty results.

```sh
python -m uados --project . task record TASK_ID --session SESSION_ID \
  --summary "What changed, why, and what validation established" \
  --evidence evidence/validation.txt
```

For protocol-2 major work, open a result debate with `debate open TASK_ID --roles ROLE_PLAN_ID --stage result --session SESSION_ID` over submitted current work. Complete its rounds so consensus records current independent result approvals from eligible reviewer votes. For legacy major work, use the recorded independent result-review gate. Review approval must include a concrete challenge and readable evidence. Task, scope, policy, source, role assignment, declared capability and evidence changes can stale the relevant approval or consensus; renew the required records instead of relabeling or dropping dissent.

Run a final audit. Complete only when acceptance criteria, unchanged evidence and all applicable current approvals are satisfied. If important uncertainty remains, record a blocker, owned follow-up or explicit limitation. Hashes establish content consistency, not authenticity or proof that the conclusion follows.

## 5. Research branch

Apply the same lifecycle in research and hybrid projects. Follow [innovation policy](RESEARCH_MANAGEMENT/innovation_policy.md), reproducibility, data-management and publication rules. Register literature with stable source identifiers and truthful `full_text`, `abstract` or `unavailable` access. Capture search coverage and exclusion reasons; unavailable access does not show absence of prior work.

Record research ideas with existing work, current limitation, scientific gap, proposed innovation, why prior methods cannot solve it, expected contribution and publication potential. Register a separate falsifiable hypothesis: prediction, rejection criterion and testing method. Protocol-2 scientific experiments link the idea and hypothesis records; explicitly operational-only executions may omit a hypothesis and cannot support a scientific outcome. A provisional candidate novelty verdict needs at least two distinct full-text sources, coverage evidence and an independent evidence-backed audit. Preserve `overlap` and `inconclusive` outcomes; no verdict proves global novelty or publication acceptance.

Before a run, register an explicit JSON argument vector, configuration, dataset manifests, seed, working directory and relevant scope with `experiment add`. Inspect the invoked program and use `experiment run EXPERIMENT_ID --timeout SECONDS --session SESSION_ID`. Programs run with the user's privileges; seed metadata does not cause the program to apply it.

Keep raw output and structured analysis. After execution, refresh and acknowledge, then record scientific interpretation with `experiment conclude`. Distinguish process failure, an invalid experiment, a valid negative finding and an inconclusive result. Verify input/environment availability before a replication claim; contributors supply validity and statistics that the CLI cannot infer.

## 6. Close with a usable handover

Follow [.agent/handover_protocol.md](.agent/handover_protocol.md). Update task records, decisions, notes and evidence, then close the session so UADOS generates `SESSION_HANDOVER.md`.

```sh
python -m uados --project . session close SESSION_ID \
  --summary "Current status, completed work and validation" \
  --next "First concrete next action with task/evidence paths"
```

Add repeatable `--blocker` and `--failed` fields when real issues exist. Preserve remaining tasks, known problems, important decisions, failed approaches and recommended next actions. Close releases unfinished task leases while retaining contributor history. A new contributor must verify the handover against current files and ledger rather than assuming old resources remain available.

## 7. Audit and improve

Run `audit` before consequential review, at handover and after copying/restoring a workspace. Its normal operation is read-only. `audit --repair` regenerates projections from a valid ledger; it does not repair evidence, change scientific conclusions or erase history. `audit --record --session SESSION_ID` can create deduplicated proposed improvements in `SYSTEM_IMPROVEMENT_LOG.md`; it does not automatically execute a fix. Diagnostic audit recording may use an already acknowledged session whose context has since become stale, because it authorizes no implementation; refresh is still required before tracked work.

An improvement records problem, root cause (or explicitly unknown cause), proposed improvement, implementation status and future prevention. Follow `ENGINEERING_RULES/extensions.md` to turn it into owned, reviewed, validated work. Preserve original failures and lessons. Stronger external identity, provider dispatch, distributed coordination and authenticated audit anchors require separate integrations.


For a manually investigated improvement, `improvement --record evidence/improvement.json --session SESSION_ID` accepts string fields `problem`, `root_cause`, `improvement`, `implementation`, `prevention` and an `evidence` array of readable project-relative paths. State an unknown root cause explicitly. The record remains proposed work; implement a fix through its own task and review process. Use `adapter --runtime Codex --agent AGENT_ID` (or the CLI's other runtime choices) to obtain a read-only bootstrap/context packet, not to launch the named client.


Record validation results to a new, versioned artifact path. Never overwrite a file after a task, review, change, experiment or debate has referenced its bytes; record a new result and obtain the required current review. UADOS archives exact registered bytes, but current-path drift still invalidates active approvals. Audit distinguishes current consistency from historical original-byte availability; inspect both `ok` and `history_ok`, and preserve reported historical loss honestly.

# Multi-agent collaboration

UADOS coordinates contributors through durable tasks, scoped ownership, review records and session handovers. It does not need a particular model provider or orchestration service. The human or agent environment chooses how to start independent contributors; each contributor uses the same project record.

The lifecycle authority is `MASTER_AGENT_WORKFLOW.md`. Read `roles.md` for responsibilities and `review_protocol.md` for substantive review. Protocol-2 major work uses `role_generator.md`, `agent_selection.md`, `debate_protocol.md` and `consensus_protocol.md`. Generated `role_plans.md` and root `CONSENSUS_DECISION.md` record the current plan/debates. A team can combine roles transparently; role count does not replace the independent reviewer quorum.

Before assigning work, make a task with a concrete outcome, relevant paths, risk and dependencies. Contributors inspect current context and claim their tasks. Keep parallel scopes disjoint where possible. Active claims with overlapping declared scopes are rejected; scope-less tasks cannot provide file-level coordination. A task lease is a recorded ownership mechanism rather than an operating-system access restriction.

Communication that changes project direction must become a decision, task or note. A reviewer should leave an evidence-backed challenge instead of an untraceable approval in chat. Before a contributor leaves, close the session with current findings and a usable next step.

The team remains responsible for real independence. Creating several labels in one process does not satisfy adversarial review. Record actual reviewer ownership, inspected artifacts and assumptions challenged so a human can assess quality. UADOS selects registered declared capabilities and exports agent-neutral dispatch packets; an authorized host supplies actual independent contributors. It does not call model providers automatically.

# Capability-based agent selection

Lifecycle authority: [MASTER_AGENT_WORKFLOW.md](../MASTER_AGENT_WORKFLOW.md). Register stable contributor identity, client/provider metadata if known and declared capabilities before assigning generated roles. Do not claim a capability because a model's marketing label implies it.

Match each role's required capabilities to registered declarations. Explain assignments and uncovered requirements. Implementation and review ownership must remain visible when several roles are assigned to one person/model. Task authors and current/past implementers are ineligible as independent reviewers; handover or renaming does not erase that history.

Before debate, verify full role coverage and the master's independent reviewer quorum. Freeze assignments, participant identities and capabilities in the debate input snapshot. Changes to task/policy/source/evidence, live assignments or capabilities can invalidate the debate; restart or renew it using the CLI's current controls.

The dispatch packet is provider-neutral JSON containing assignments, instructions, task/context and evidence references. It can be delivered by an authorized host to independent contributors. UADOS does not call paid APIs, provision credentials, spawn commercial clients or authenticate that contributors are different models. Actual dispatch, independence and cost authorization belong to the host/team.

# Consensus and dissent

Lifecycle authority: [MASTER_AGENT_WORKFLOW.md](../MASTER_AGENT_WORKFLOW.md). `CONSENSUS_DECISION.md` is generated from recorded debates. Do not create a manually approved substitute.

A consensus identifies the selected Round-1 analysis, selected approach, rejected alternatives and reasons, remaining risks, participants, role ownership, challenges, votes and evidence. The selected approach must correspond to a real analysis in that debate. Record unresolved objections; a report that drops dissent cannot justify the master's review gate.

Consensus requires complete ordered rounds and current bound inputs. Consensus records independent plan/result approvals from eligible reviewer votes, bound to the current task fingerprint. A manually written consensus report does not substitute for those governed approvals. At least two eligible independent reviewers are required for a protocol-2 major debate, even when one reviewer covers several roles. The actual human/model independence remains a team responsibility.

A requested change prevents treating the debate as approved until the required renewed process resolves it. Do not relabel an implementer, replace a participant or summarize away an objection to manufacture approval. Keep earlier debate outcomes visible when a new debate is opened. Changed task, policy, scope, source, assignments, capabilities or evidence requires the CLI's staleness checks and renewed review.

Remaining risks need an explicit disposition: accepted within authority, validated, blocked pending evidence, or assigned follow-up. Consensus is a traceable local decision, not distributed fault-tolerant consensus or a guarantee of a correct technical/scientific conclusion.

# Adversarial debate protocol

Lifecycle authority: [MASTER_AGENT_WORKFLOW.md](../MASTER_AGENT_WORKFLOW.md). A protocol-2 major task uses a plan debate before claim and a result debate over submitted implementation before completion. The CLI stores staged contributions and content fingerprints; participants supply substantive reasoning and actual independence.

## Round 1: independent analysis

Every assigned participant submits its own proposed solution, assumptions, risks and evidence. Inspect the underlying task, change request, plan or result, scoped files and relevant policies. Analyze independently before reading endorsements from others where the host supports that isolation. Explain a plausible alternative and the observation that could make it preferable.

## Round 2: adversarial challenge

Every participant challenges an analysis by another participant with a concrete failure mechanism and evidence. Ask why the proposal could fail, which assumptions are unsupported, what alternatives exist and which evidence is missing. Address compatibility, resource access, recovery and research validity where applicable.

Complete analysis before challenge, and challenge before voting. Round inputs, analyses and challenges are immutable; rework requires a new recorded debate rather than editing those submissions. During the vote round a contributor may append a reasoned replacement ballot; all earlier votes remain visible. Do not remove dissent by changing the participant set.

## Round 3: vote and consensus

Each participant votes on the selected analysis with reason and evidence. Use the CLI's explicit vote vocabulary; a request for changes is not an approval. Consensus records the selected analysis ID, approach, rejected alternatives, reasoning, remaining risks and preserved participant votes/challenges. See [consensus_protocol.md](consensus_protocol.md).

Bind the debate to the current task and relevant source/policy/evidence plus role assignments and declared capabilities. For result review, include the actual submitted work revision. If these inputs change, do not reuse stale approval. A participant who detects a blocker should request changes and name the missing evidence or recovery step.


## CLI contribution forms

Use issued IDs and actual supporting evidence. Every mutating form takes the contributor's currently acknowledged session. Repeat analysis assumption/risk/alternative/evidence flags as needed.

```sh
python -m uados --project . debate analysis DEBATE_ID --session SESSION_ID \
  --solution "Independent proposed approach" --assumption "Explicit assumption" \
  --risk "Concrete failure mode" --alternative "Reasoned alternative" \
  --evidence evidence/analysis.md
python -m uados --project . debate advance DEBATE_ID --session SESSION_ID
python -m uados --project . debate challenge DEBATE_ID --session SESSION_ID \
  --target OTHER_ANALYSIS_ID --failure "How this could fail" \
  --unsupported "Unsupported assumption" --alternative "Better choice under stated conditions" \
  --missing-evidence "What would resolve the challenge" --evidence evidence/challenge.md
python -m uados --project . debate advance DEBATE_ID --session SESSION_ID
python -m uados --project . debate vote DEBATE_ID --session SESSION_ID \
  --select SELECTED_ANALYSIS_ID --verdict approve --reason "Evidence-backed disposition of challenges" \
  --evidence evidence/review.md
python -m uados --project . debate consensus DEBATE_ID --session SESSION_ID \
  --select SELECTED_ANALYSIS_ID --reason "Selection and rejected alternatives" \
  --risk "Remaining risk and its disposition"
```

Advance succeeds only when all participants have completed the current contribution round. Other participants must submit their own records; this sample shows forms for one contributor, not a one-agent debate. Use `--verdict request_changes` for an unresolved objection. Consensus requires all current votes to approve the same actual analysis and the independent quorum; prior objections remain in history. Consensus also generates bound independent approval records from eligible reviewer ballots.

# Independent adversarial review

Lifecycle authority: `MASTER_AGENT_WORKFLOW.md`. This document explains review substance for both recorded protocols. Protocol-2 major tasks additionally use the staged `debate_protocol.md` and `consensus_protocol.md`; legacy task approvals keep their recorded interpretation. Recorded consensus generates current independent plan/result approval records from eligible reviewer votes; a manually written report does not substitute for them.

The review question is: what plausible failure, missing assumption or better alternative could change the decision? The reviewer must inspect evidence rather than merely restating the implementer's explanation.

## Plan review

Before a major task is claimed, the implementer provides a plan covering problem, acceptance criteria, alternatives, scope, dependencies, validation, risks and recovery. The reviewer starts and acknowledges an independent session, reads relevant context and tests the plan's assumptions.

Examine at least the consequential risks: incomplete requirements, hidden shared state, compatibility, failure recovery, security/data boundaries, resource cost or experimental validity. Identify a falsifiable challenge, such as a migration that could lose records or a dataset split that could leak labels. Explain why the plan addresses the challenge or which change is required.

Record the review:

```sh
python -m uados --project . task review TASK_ID --session REVIEW_SESSION_ID \
  --stage plan --verdict approve \
  --challenge "Specific assumption tested and resulting judgment" \
  --evidence evidence/plan-review.md
```

Use `request_changes` when the plan lacks evidence or needs revision. Approval authorizes the planned tracked lifecycle; it does not grant external deployment, spending or data-sharing permission.

## Result review

After implementation and evidence recording, inspect the actual task, scoped files and result evidence. Compare the result with the approved plan and acceptance criteria. Reproduce a meaningful check when feasible, or explain why the review relies on supplied evidence. Do not mark an unavailable check as passing.

Record the same fields with `--stage result`. A major task's completion requires a current approved result by a distinct agent identity. The result review binds the reviewed task, scoped content and evidence fingerprint. Later edits to those inputs require a new result review; an older approval is not a blank authorization.

## Review record quality

Use `TEMPLATES/review.md`. Include inspected paths/revision, the strongest plausible challenge, findings with severity and evidence, verdict and unresolved limitations. An empty statement such as “looks good” does not preserve reasoning.

A second label cannot establish actual independence. The human team chooses a separate contributor or review process and verifies that the reviewer did not author the result. The CLI can check label inequality and recorded lifecycle conditions; it cannot prove who controlled a process.

## Disagreement and resolution

Keep objections and evidence visible. The implementer may revise the proposal, provide new evidence or record a trade-off for the human owner. Do not erase a rejected review to manufacture consensus. If a dispute blocks completion, record the task blocker and the specific decision or experiment needed to resolve it.

## Contributor history and independent review

Claiming a task preserves the contributor identity across handovers. A task author or any current or previous implementation contributor cannot supply its independent plan or result approval. Changing sessions or handing implementation to another agent does not erase that conflict of interest. Reviewer labels still require trusted human attribution.

# Dynamic role generation

Lifecycle authority: [MASTER_AGENT_WORKFLOW.md](../MASTER_AGENT_WORKFLOW.md). Role generation turns task text, project mode and explicit task-type override into a review/implementation coverage plan. Task risk determines lifecycle depth under the master workflow. It is deterministic local planning, not autonomous model creation.

Generation uses the task's title/description, project mode and optional explicit type. Inspect risk and scope separately to assess coverage. Generate roles with concrete responsibilities and declared capability requirements. Inspect the generated plan for domain omissions; a title keyword is evidence of a likely need, not proof that the selected team is sufficient.

| Task family | Example coverage |
| --- | --- |
| Software database/performance | Architecture, implementation/backend, performance, security and testing |
| Research biosensor/materials | Principal investigation, literature, materials/domain expertise, experimental design, novelty and publication |
| Hybrid | Software correctness and research validity, with explicit responsibility for their interface |

The actual role list is in generated `role_plans.md`; examples do not prescribe a fixed team for every project. Choose registered contributors using [agent_selection.md](agent_selection.md). One contributor may transparently cover several roles when capabilities fit. Role count never substitutes for the independent reviewer quorum required by the master workflow.

If the task or coverage changes, regenerate/reassign before the next debate. A debate uses a fixed participant and assignment snapshot; do not change membership mid-round to remove an inconvenient challenge. Specialized domain capabilities are declarations requiring team verification.

# Roles and ownership

Lifecycle authority: `MASTER_AGENT_WORKFLOW.md`. These responsibility descriptions support the dynamic coverage process in `role_generator.md` and capability selection in `agent_selection.md`; they do not prescribe a fixed role roster for every task.

| Role | Responsibility | Durable output |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Coordinator | Translate the objective into owned tasks, dependencies and resource decisions | Task records, prioritization rationale and handover |
| Implementer | Understand context, claim work, make the change and validate it | Implementation, task evidence and technical notes |
| Architect | Examine boundaries, contracts and long-term consequences | ADR or RFC with alternatives and risks |
| Researcher | Frame hypotheses, design experiments and interpret results | Protocol, experiment records, analysis and negative findings |
| Reviewer | Challenge assumptions independently and inspect the plan or result | Review verdict, challenge and supporting evidence |
| Quality / security specialist | Investigate failures and domain-specific risks | Reproducers, findings and bounded mitigations |
| Human owner | Set priorities and authorize actions beyond contributor authority | Explicit project direction and recorded decisions |

Roles are responsibilities, not permissions automatically provisioned by UADOS. Agent labels identify records; authentication and authority remain team policy or external integrations.

## Ownership contract

An implementer owns an active task's recorded work and evidence. A reviewer owns the review judgment, not the implementation. The coordinator owns conflict resolution and dependency ordering. If an essential owner leaves, another contributor must inspect current context and explicitly take over through the available task lifecycle; do not impersonate the departed contributor.

Claims prevent another session from owning the same task while its lease is active and reject overlapping declared scopes across active tasks, including directory/child paths. Scope-less routine tasks cannot provide file-level coordination. Do not assume a file is protected from direct edits. Keep shared policy and central architecture changes out of parallel scopes unless contributors have agreed how to sequence them.

## Delegation packet

A useful delegation contains task ID, objective, acceptance criteria, risk, scope, dependencies, relevant decisions and evidence paths, resource constraints and the expected handover. Delegate a coherent responsibility. The receiving contributor should report assumptions and conflicts before doing dependent work.

Do not delegate a request for endorsement. Ask the reviewer to identify a concrete way the proposal might fail, inspect the relevant artifacts and give a reasoned verdict.

## Contributor history and independent review

Claiming a task preserves the contributor identity across handovers. A task author or any current or previous implementation contributor cannot supply its independent plan or result approval. Changing sessions or handing implementation to another agent does not erase that conflict of interest. Reviewer labels still require trusted human attribution.

# Project memory

Memory belongs to the project, independent of a contributor's model, chat or machine. A new contributor should be able to reconstruct what was attempted, what worked, what failed and why the next step follows.

## What goes where

| Knowledge | Record |
| --- | --- |
| Objective, mode, phase and work state | Generated `PROJECT_STATE.md` |
| Architecture, boundaries and resource assumptions | Maintained `architecture.md` |
| Structured tasks, dependencies and ownership | Generated `tasks.md`, edited through CLI commands |
| Significant choices and alternatives | `decision add`, projected into `DECISION_RECORD.md` |
| Technical explanations, lessons and failures | `note` projected into `knowledge.md`, or maintained `notes/*.md` |
| Experiments and execution records | `RESEARCH_MANAGEMENT/experiments.md` through the experiment commands |
| Session stopping point | `session close`, projected into `SESSION_HANDOVER.md` |
| Detailed proof of a claim | An evidence artifact linked to its task, decision or review |

Create `notes/` when needed. Name notes by subject or stable identifier. A durable note should include its source, date or event, scope, conclusion, uncertainty and the next decision it affects. Link to local evidence and relevant task or experiment IDs. Avoid duplicating mutable task status in several documents.

## Memory quality

Describe evidence strength explicitly: observed, inferred, proposed or unverified. Preserve rejected alternatives and the condition under which they might become useful. An error without its command and inputs is rarely a useful failure record.

Prefer relative paths inside the project so memory survives copying. For external or restricted resources, store a manifest containing a stable identifier, version, checksum if available, access conditions and retrieval instructions. Do not pretend those resources were included in a project export.

No conversation should be the sole record of a consequential decision. Capture such knowledge before closing the session. Maintained notes are context inputs; edit them deliberately, and refresh an affected session before further tracked work.

`knowledge.md` and `session_reports/` are generated from the ledger. Preserve them through the recorded note/session lifecycle rather than hand-editing their contents.

# Bootstrap prompt

You are a new contributor to this UADOS project. Establish context before modifying implementation or running a substantive experiment.

Read `MASTER_AGENT_WORKFLOW.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `PROJECT_STATE.md`, `SESSION_HANDOVER.md`, `PROJECT_MEMORY/`, `DEVELOPMENT_LOG.md`, `DECISION_RECORD.md` and relevant engineering/research rules. Inspect underlying evidence for the area you will work on. Identify missing resources and assumptions without inventing facts.

Start a session with `python -m uados --project . session start --agent <stable contributor label>`. Read the printed Understanding Report and its listed source documents. Check objective, phase, architecture, completed work, problems, risks, resources and recommended next actions. Acknowledge the printed session ID and exact report hash only after that inspection.

Explain the next concrete task, its acceptance criteria, risk, scope and dependencies. Reuse an appropriate existing task or create one through the CLI. Obtain independent plan approval for major work before claim. If context changes, refresh and acknowledge the new report before further tracked work.

Preserve important reasoning in decisions and notes, attach meaningful evidence, and close the session with a handover. Keep implementation edits and maintained notes separate from generated projections. Treat the CLI's acknowledgements and agent labels as workflow records, not proof of comprehension or identity.

# Independent challenge prompt

Review task `<TASK_ID>` at stage `<plan or result>` independently from its author and implementer. Your goal is to identify a concrete way the proposal could fail or its conclusion could be unsupported.

Start an independent session with your stable contributor label, inspect current context and acknowledge the report hash. Read the relevant plan or result, scoped files, evidence, acceptance criteria and governing rules. Do not accept the implementer's summary as sufficient proof.

Choose the strongest plausible challenge: a hidden assumption, boundary/failure case, security or data-integrity issue, incompatible interface, unfair baseline, leakage, confounding or alternative explanation. Investigate it with relevant evidence or a check. Identify findings that could materially change the decision and distinguish observations from uncertainty.

Write a review artifact using `TEMPLATES/review.md`. State what was inspected and what was unavailable; never claim to have run an unexecuted check. Give `approve` or `request_changes` with a concrete reason and challenge. Record it using `task review TASK_ID --stage ... --verdict ... --challenge ... --evidence ... --session ...`.

Use a label distinct from the task's author and implementer. Real independence is a team obligation; choosing a different string does not establish it. A result approval applies to current task, scoped files and evidence, and must be renewed after consequential edits.

# Handover prompt

Prepare to stop work so another contributor can resume without this conversation.

Check recorded state against actual files. Record untracked consequential reasoning as decisions or notes, preserve task/experiment validation artifacts and identify incomplete work. Do not manufacture completion to make the handover appear clean.

Summarize completed outcomes and their evidence. Explain the current stopping point, active or released work, remaining acceptance gaps, unavailable resources, known risks and failed approaches. For failures, retain the command, configuration, observed result and why repeating it blindly is unhelpful.

Choose an ordered next action with task ID, relevant path, exact check or procedure and expected outcome. Name any unresolved decision or authority requirement. Use `TEMPLATES/handover.md` for supporting detail, then close the session through `session close` with summary and at least one `--next`; include applicable `--blocker` and `--failed` fields.

The CLI generates `SESSION_HANDOVER.md`. Keep longer maintained explanations in project notes and reference them. Run an audit and report material failures honestly. A new contributor must inspect a fresh Understanding Report before acting.

# Implementation prompt

Continue task `<TASK_ID>` in scope `<PATHS>` with acceptance criteria `<CRITERIA>`. Follow the current UADOS workflow and applicable project rules.

Before acting, inspect the task, its dependencies, relevant decisions, current implementation and evidence. Start or refresh a session, read its Understanding Report and acknowledge its current hash. Verify required resources. Claim the task; major work must already have an independent approved plan.

Implement the smallest coherent change satisfying the task. Respect other contributors' ownership. If assumptions or scope change materially, document the change and obtain renewed plan review instead of continuing under an obsolete plan. Record consequential choices with problem, alternatives, evidence, reason and risk.

Run checks that actually test the changed behavior. Preserve outputs and explain what they establish and what they leave uncertain. Record the task result with its evidence. Do not call an unavailable or unexecuted check passing. Major work requires independent result approval for the current scoped content/evidence before completion.

If blocked, record the cause, evidence and concrete recovery action. Preserve failed approaches and lessons. At a stopping point, close the session with completed work, validation, unresolved gaps and the first action for a new contributor. Do not hand-edit generated state or log files.

# Research prompt

Investigate question `<QUESTION>` under the project's UADOS research workflow. Establish and acknowledge current context before designing or running substantive work.

Read relevant literature records, decisions, hypotheses, dataset manifests and experiment results. Describe source coverage and access limits; do not invent references or interpret an unavailable source as empty. Define a falsifiable hypothesis, baseline, controls, outcome metrics, units and threats to validity. Review costly or consequential work independently before execution.

Create an execution packet with command JSON argument array, working directory, configuration, dataset/manifests, code scope, seed handling, runtime dependencies and resource limits. Register it using `experiment add`; ensure the program actually applies recorded seeds. Inspect executable inputs because `experiment run` is not a sandbox.

Run with a suitable timeout and preserve raw output. Refresh and acknowledge context after the recorded run. Interpret observations using a maintained analysis artifact and `experiment conclude`; distinguish process success from a supported scientific conclusion, valid negative result, invalid run or operational failure.

Report repetitions, variability and uncertainty appropriate to the claim. Preserve alternative explanations, failures and negative findings. Keep restricted data under authorized access; FAIR metadata does not authorize public sharing. Close with evidence and a concrete next experiment or decision.

# UADOS project workspace

UADOS keeps a project's decisions, tasks, evidence and handovers inside the project so another human or agent can continue the work. This scaffold supports software, research and hybrid projects. The Python CLI records structured work; the maintained documents explain how the team should carry it out.

Start with `MASTER_AGENT_WORKFLOW.md`, `PROJECT_STATE.md`, `SESSION_HANDOVER.md`, `DEVELOPMENT_LOG.md`, `DECISION_RECORD.md` and `PROJECT_MEMORY/`. Then read the rules for the work you plan to perform.

## Two kinds of project files

The authoritative record is `.uados/ledger.sqlite3`. UADOS commits current state and its hash-chained event together in one SQLite transaction. It generates these readable projections from that record:

- `PROJECT_STATE.md`: objective, mode, phase, work and blockers.
- `DEVELOPMENT_LOG.md`: durable action history.
- `DECISION_RECORD.md`: problems, alternatives, decisions and reasons.
- `SESSION_HANDOVER.md`: the latest recorded stopping point and next actions.
- `PROJECT_MEMORY/tasks.md`, `PROJECT_MEMORY/knowledge.md` and `RESEARCH_MANAGEMENT/experiments.md`: structured tasks, recorded notes and experiment records.
- `PROJECT_MEMORY/session_reports/`: issued Understanding Reports.
- `.uados/state.json` and `.uados/events.jsonl`: machine-readable projections.
- `CONSENSUS_DECISION.md`, `MULTI_AGENT_SYSTEM/role_plans.md` and `CHANGE_REQUESTS/CR*.md` records: role, debate and change views. The maintained `CR_TEMPLATE.md` is the exception.
- `RESEARCH_MANAGEMENT/LITERATURE_GAP_ANALYSIS.md`, `NOVELTY_AUDIT.md`, `RESEARCH_DECISION_RECORD.md` and `HYPOTHESES.md`: literature, idea and provisional novelty views.
- `SYSTEM_IMPROVEMENT_LOG.md`: proposed audit improvements and recorded disposition.

Do not edit those generated files manually. Use the CLI to change their source record. Write free-form knowledge in `PROJECT_MEMORY/notes/` or maintained policies, and link evidence through tracked actions. `audit --repair` rebuilds projections; it does not repair a damaged ledger or recover missing evidence.
