documents.RESEARCH_MANAGEMENT/innovation_policy.md:
# Research innovation and novelty policy

Lifecycle authority: [MASTER_AGENT_WORKFLOW.md](../MASTER_AGENT_WORKFLOW.md). Innovation is a falsifiable research proposition grounded in known work and access limits. An audit simulates critical peer review; it cannot certify universal novelty or guarantee publication.

## Literature and access

Register each source with a stable source identifier, primary HTTP(S) location, relevance, limitations, observed access level, corpus group and supporting evidence. Registration does not fetch the URL. Use `full_text`, `abstract` or `unavailable` truthfully. Two records of the same source do not count as two independent prior works. Record retrieval/search scope, dates, queries, exclusions and unresolved access in coverage evidence. A failed search source is unavailable, not an empty literature result.

Keep copyrighted/restricted material within authorized access. Store manifests and permissible summaries when raw sources cannot be distributed. A local hash proves byte consistency, not that the source says what the summary claims.

## Idea and hypothesis

Every idea contains these seven fields:

| Field | Review question |
| --- | --- |
| Existing Work | Which specific prior studies are the strongest baseline? |
| Current Limitation | What observed limitation remains under which conditions? |
| Scientific Gap | Which unresolved scientific question follows from that evidence? |
| Proposed Innovation | What mechanism or method changes, and how can it be tested? |
| Why Previous Methods Cannot Solve It | Which assumption or demonstrated boundary defeats the alternatives? |
| Expected Contribution | What measurable knowledge/result would the study add? |
| Publication Potential | Which audience could benefit, with what uncertainty and required evidence? |

Register falsifiable hypotheses separately and link them to the idea. A hypothesis specifies a prediction, an observation that would reject it and a testing method. Broad aspirations and a successful process exit are not hypotheses. Protocol-2 scientific experiments link both idea and hypothesis IDs while preserving command, input/config/data/code/environment evidence. An explicitly operational-only execution may omit a hypothesis, but its run cannot support a scientific supported/refuted outcome.

## Independent novelty audit

An eligible independent reviewer inspects the idea, source contents, access limitations and search coverage. Record a reasoned verdict:

- `candidate`: provisionally plausible contribution within recorded coverage; requires at least two distinct full-text sources from distinct corpus groups and coverage evidence. Every supporting source linked to a candidate idea must have full-text access; abstract-only/unavailable support cannot be silently counted.
- `overlap`: prior work materially overlaps; identify it and explain whether a narrower claim remains testable.
- `inconclusive`: evidence, access or coverage is insufficient; name what could resolve the uncertainty.

Source/idea/policy/evidence changes can make an audit stale. Renew the audit rather than presenting old evidence as current. Record hypothesis tests and interpretation separately; process failures, invalid runs, valid negative findings and inconclusive scientific results must remain distinguishable.

Generated `LITERATURE_GAP_ANALYSIS.md`, `NOVELTY_AUDIT.md`, `RESEARCH_DECISION_RECORD.md` and `HYPOTHESES.md` are ledger projections. Use research operations to update them. Candidate novelty remains provisional even after a clean local audit; external peer review, broad literature coverage and domain-valid experiments are future evidence, not implied by these records.


## Structured input shapes

These are schema examples, not retrieved sources or scientific findings. Replace placeholders, verify access and create readable evidence before using `research source --record evidence/source.json --session SESSION_ID`, `research idea --record evidence/idea.json --session SESSION_ID` and `research hypothesis --record evidence/hypothesis.json --session SESSION_ID`. Use issued source/idea/hypothesis IDs.

```json
{
  "title": "Source title",
  "identifier": "Stable primary source identifier",
  "url": "https://example.org/replace-with-primary-source",
  "claim": "Permissible evidence-backed summary",
  "limitation": "Limit of access or method",
  "access": "unavailable",
  "corpus": "Distinct primary work or corpus group",
  "evidence": ["evidence/source-access.md"]
}
```

The default unavailable value illustrates honest access recording; it cannot support candidate novelty. Use `full_text` only after actual access. Two sections/URLs from one handbook or corpus are not distinct corpus coverage.

```json
{
  "title": "Testable proposed contribution",
  "fields": {
    "existing_work": "Specific strongest prior work",
    "current_limitation": "Observed boundary and conditions",
    "scientific_gap": "Unresolved question grounded in evidence",
    "proposed_innovation": "Testable proposed mechanism",
    "prior_methods_insufficient": "Evidence-backed reason alternatives fail",
    "expected_contribution": "Measurable new result or knowledge",
    "publication_potential": "Audience, uncertainty and required evidence",
    "coverage_limit": "Search/retrieval scope and missing work"
  },
  "sources": ["SOURCE_ID_1", "SOURCE_ID_2"],
  "evidence": ["evidence/coverage-and-analysis.md"]
}
```

`coverage_limit` is an additional mandatory scope disclosure alongside the seven innovation fields.

```json
{
  "idea": "IDEA_ID",
  "prediction": "Falsifiable expected effect under stated conditions",
  "baseline": "Comparator and controls",
  "metric": "Measurement, units and experimental unit",
  "rejection": "Observation or threshold that rejects the prediction",
  "uncertainty": "Replication, variability and known confounds",
  "evidence": ["evidence/experimental-design.md"]
}
```

Use `experiment add ... --hypothesis-id HYPOTHESIS_ID` with its complete command/config/dataset/seed/scope packet. After inspecting a resolved run and refreshing context, use `research outcome HYPOTHESIS_ID --experiment EXPERIMENT_ID --run RUN_ID --verdict supported|refuted|inconclusive --reason ... --evidence ... --session SESSION_ID`. Choose one verdict value. Failed/interrupted/invalidated execution can support only an inconclusive operational outcome, not a scientific supported/refuted finding. `experiment conclude` preserves the detailed scientific interpretation separately.
documents.RESEARCH_MANAGEMENT/publication.md:
# Literature, novelty and publication

## Literature record

Use `TEMPLATES/literature.md` to record the research question, search sources and query, dates, inclusion criteria and coverage limits. Preserve verified identifiers and links for relevant work, with claims, methods, datasets, limitations and the relationship to this project.

Do not invent references, metrics or missing details. Distinguish reading the full text from relying on an abstract or secondary description. If a source is unavailable, say so and avoid attributing unsupported conclusions to it. Respect source licenses and quotation limits.

## Novelty assessment

Compare the proposed contribution with the closest relevant work, including strong baselines and alternative explanations. State what is new, what is reused and where the evidence is incomplete. Literature coverage is bounded by the search method and date; “no matching result found” is not proof that no prior work exists.

Record changes in the research direction as reasoned decisions. Preserve rejected hypotheses and unsuccessful attempts when they influence interpretation or prevent repeated work.

## Claim-to-evidence mapping

Before submission, map every material claim to experiment IDs, raw outputs, analysis procedures and relevant sources. Verify that figures and tables reproduce from those artifacts, use consistent units and state uncertainty. Keep failed and negative findings available; do not selectively report only favorable runs.

For hybrid projects, record the code revision that produced results and distinguish a prototype demonstration from a validated general capability. Explain limitations, dataset coverage, threats to validity and replication conditions.

## Submission review

Have an independent reviewer challenge novelty, experimental design, baseline fairness, leakage, statistical interpretation and reproducibility. Resolve unsupported claims or mark them as hypotheses. Check the intended venue's current formatting, artifact, authorship and ethics requirements separately; UADOS does not encode changing venue rules.

Publication and external data sharing require the project's authorized owner's decision. The local record supports preparation and review; it does not publish a manuscript or provision a repository automatically.
documents.RESEARCH_MANAGEMENT/reproducibility.md:
# Reproducible experiments

## Protocol before execution

Use `TEMPLATES/experiment.md` to state question, hypothesis, baseline, controls, measurements, units, sample design and analysis. Distinguish exploratory analysis from a confirmatory test. Define exclusion and stopping criteria before examining outcomes when those criteria affect inference.

Record the command as a JSON array of arguments, not an informal shell fragment. For example:

```sh
python -m uados --project . experiment add --session SESSION_ID \
  --title "Evaluate the prespecified hypothesis" \
  --hypothesis "A concrete, measurable prediction" \
  --command-json '["python3", "experiment.py", "--config", "config.json"]' \
  --config config.json --dataset data/manifest.json --seed 7 \
  --scope experiment.py --cwd .
```

Repeat dataset and scope arguments when appropriate. Check the actual CLI help for required fields. Recording a seed as metadata does not ensure the invoked program uses it: pass it in configuration or arguments and verify the relevant libraries honor it.

Run the registered experiment:

```sh
python -m uados --project . experiment run EXPERIMENT_ID \
  --session SESSION_ID --timeout 300
```

The executable runs with the contributor's privileges, without an execution sandbox. Inspect the program and its command before running.

Run completion changes recorded context. Refresh the session, inspect the new report and acknowledge its hash before adding an interpretation or further tracked work. Record the scientific conclusion separately:

```sh
python -m uados --project . experiment conclude EXPERIMENT_ID \
  --session SESSION_ID \
  --conclusion "Observed result, uncertainty and implications for the hypothesis" \
  --evidence evidence/analysis.md
```

## Reproduction packet

Keep enough material to repeat and interpret the run:

- Exact command, working directory, configuration and versioned input manifests.
- Code revision and relevant file fingerprints.
- Runtime, dependency versions, operating system and instrument or hardware details.
- Data provenance, preprocessing, splits and access conditions.
- Seed handling, nondeterministic operations and known sources of variation.
- Exit status, raw outputs, metrics and the analysis procedure.
- Budget, duration, timeout and incomplete-run handling.

The CLI records selected inputs; the researcher must identify other influential resources. An external service, changing dataset or unavailable instrument may prevent exact repetition. Label these limits and provide a feasible replication procedure instead of asserting full reproducibility.

## Analysis and uncertainty

Use metrics that answer the hypothesis, include baselines, and report units. Where appropriate, report repetitions, variability, confidence intervals, effect sizes and the analysis assumptions. Avoid interpreting one favorable seed as a general conclusion. Track multiple comparisons, model selection and exploratory choices that could bias the claim.

Distinguish operational failure from a valid negative result. A timeout, missing input or numerical error usually makes the run incomplete or invalid. A valid result contradicting the hypothesis is useful evidence and must remain in memory.

## Replication and drift

Before rerunning, compare code, config, data and environment with the original packet. Explain differences rather than silently overwriting old outputs. Retain separate records for reruns. If inputs drift, the new run answers a potentially different question; revise the conclusion and review scope accordingly.

If a launcher disappeared while a run remains recorded as `running`, inspect whether the process is still alive and preserve partial outputs. Once the execution has stopped, use `experiment resolve EXPERIMENT_ID --session SESSION_ID --reason ...` to record interrupted-run recovery before retrying. This command records your recovery judgment; it does not discover or terminate an unknown surviving process automatically.

documents.VERSION_CONTROL/README.md:
# Version control and delivery

Use version control to preserve implementation and maintained documents alongside the UADOS record. UADOS is local and does not create remote repositories, configure protected branches, run hosted CI or deploy software.

## Team workflow

Use a branch or worktree for concurrent implementation where appropriate. Associate changes with task IDs and keep scopes coherent. Inspect existing modifications before beginning; never reset or discard another contributor's work to obtain a clean checkout.

Before requesting review, record the task result and evidence. Review the current scoped contents and attach the relevant artifacts. A commit alone is not a UADOS completion record, and a UADOS approval does not replace remote branch protection.

Make commit messages explain the resulting behavior and its reason. Record significant design rationale as a tracked decision rather than hiding it only in commit text.

## Durable record and backups

Back up the authoritative `.uados/ledger.sqlite3`, maintained context and evidence together. Use a consistent SQLite backup or a quiescent copy; do not copy an actively written database file and assume it represents a complete transaction. Do not merge SQLite binaries by hand. For shared local work, let the CLI serialize mutations through its project lock.

For normal Git commits, version a consistent `.uados/events.jsonl`, `.uados/state.json`, generated/maintained Markdown and needed evidence. Ignore the local ledger, its transient journal files and `.uados/lock`; do not ignore all of `.uados/` if Git is your restoration method. Data/output privacy and size may require an approved artifact store with explicit restoration instructions.

After cloning a revision without the local database:

```sh
python -m uados --project . rebuild-ledger
python -m uados --project . audit
```

`rebuild-ledger` validates exported event sequence, chain and matching state before creating a missing database. It never overwrites an existing one. It cannot establish an export's authenticity. Divergent event chains from parallel Git branches cannot be reconciled by concatenating JSON lines or ordinary text conflict resolution: select a validated coherent history and record how work from the other branch is reconciled.

For a portable initialized directory, use `export PATH` to a new destination outside the source project. Repeated `--include PATH` adds other project-relative files/directories. Verify the destination's audit and the actual workload; installation, external data and unrelated dependencies are not automatically captured.

Generated Markdown and JSON are useful for human review, but are projections rather than alternative sources of truth. If a restore produces projection discrepancies, audit and regenerate from the valid ledger. Retain original artifacts until recovery has been verified.

## Optional CI and release policy

If the team configures CI, make required checks explicit and retain their commands, environment and outcomes as evidence. Avoid credentials in logs. Verify a restored project with `audit` and the relevant software/research checks.

Before release, identify the tested revision, completed tasks, known limitations, migration and rollback procedure. Inspect distributed content for private data and accidental credentials. A public release, remote push or deployment is an external action governed by project authorization, not an automatic result of recording task completion.

# ADR 0001: One local transactional ledger with rebuildable views

- Status: Accepted for UADOS v1.
- Scope: Project state, durable event history and generated memory.

## Problem

Agents need project knowledge that survives a model change, process interruption or machine handover. Several independently edited Markdown/JSON files cannot establish which state is authoritative or guarantee that a task update and its history entry commit together. A projection failure must not silently erase committed work or cause a contributor to repeat it.

## Alternatives considered

| Alternative | Benefit | Limitation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Markdown-only memory | Easy manual editing and human review | No transactional state/history boundary or enforceable lifecycle |
| Separate JSON state and append-only JSONL events as authority | Simple portable formats | Cross-file writes can diverge during interruption; concurrent writers need an additional transaction design |
| Hosted database and orchestration service | Central identity and multi-machine coordination are possible | Requires deployment, network, service administration and a broader trust/availability design |
| Local SQLite ledger with generated Markdown/JSON | Standard-library ACID transaction, inspectable record, offline operation | Local writer trust; serialized writes; external filesystem evidence is not transactional database data |

## Decision

Use `.uados/ledger.sqlite3` as the sole runtime authority. Commit an ordered hash-chained event containing the complete resulting state and the current-state row in the same SQLite transaction. Validate chain continuity and equality between final event and current state on reads. Hold a stable OS project lock across transaction and subsequent projection generation.

Generate Markdown views, current-state JSON, event JSONL and session reports from that record. Repair only these projections from a valid ledger. For a project restored from versioned text exports without its local database, provide a separate `rebuild-ledger` command that validates the chain/state and reconstructs a missing database without overwriting an existing one.

## Reason

SQLite is available in Python's standard library, supports a concrete durability boundary and needs no network service. Full-state events retain enough information for straightforward recovery and inspection. Readable projections preserve the user-facing workflow and portability while keeping source-of-truth ambiguity out of ordinary operations.

The stable lock prevents two cooperating CLI writers from committing/generating out of order. Atomic per-file writes prevent truncated projections. Keeping database transactions distinct from derived-file generation lets the system explain an already committed action and repair its views without duplicating the action.

## Evidence and verification

The implementation separates storage, project lifecycle, context rendering and research execution. Workflow tests exercise handover, major-review gates, projection failure/repair, export and validated reconstruction. The current verification report determines which tests were actually run; the architectural choice itself is not evidence that every failure path is covered.

## Risks and consequences

- Full-state event rows consume increasing storage, and complete chain validation costs grow with history. Revisit for very large projects or measured latency problems; do not prune history without an explicit retention/recovery design.
- Scope/evidence files remain outside SQLite. The lock does not stop direct editors, and retained hashes do not restore deleted artifacts. Quiesce uncooperative writers for consistent copies and back up evidence with memory.
- A hash chain is local consistency evidence, not authenticated provenance. A writer controlling the ledger can rewrite it and recompute hashes. External trusted anchors, signatures and identity require a future design.
- Git exports must represent one consistent history. Divergent chains are not safely merged by concatenating JSONL records. Preserve a selected validated chain and explicitly reconcile work.
- Projection repair cannot repair ledger corruption or establish truth from changed evidence. Preserve diagnostics and restore a verified backup or validated missing-ledger export as appropriate.
- Hosted/distributed coordination, stronger access controls and cryptographic authentication are beyond the accepted v1 boundary. Revisit when those become actual requirements.

# ADR 0002: additive workflow governance

Date: 2026-10-12. Disposition is tracked by the Phase 2 tasks and independent reviews in the ledger; this maintained document records design rationale rather than duplicating mutable task status.

## Problem and background

Phase 1 supplies working local transactional memory, acknowledged context, independent review and experiments. Static review and prose-only orchestration do not adequately record role coverage, multiple independent challenges, enterprise changes or the evidence limits of innovation claims. Phase 2 must add executable governance without erasing successful historical tasks, SHA-bound evidence or recoverable ledger events.

## Alternatives

1. Add only documents and prompts. This improves guidance but cannot validate planning, quorum, round order or evidence staleness.
2. Replace persistence and rewrite old tasks into a new schema. This creates unnecessary migration/integrity risk and falsely implies historical compliance with later rules.
3. Introduce hosted provider orchestration, authentication and distributed consensus immediately. This exceeds available identity/provider infrastructure, adds cost/authority assumptions and obscures the current cooperative local boundary.
4. Extend the existing transaction interface with explicitly versioned governance records. This retains a tested durability boundary and makes new gate/evidence behavior independently testable.

## Decision

Choose the additive design. Keep SQLite schema1 and full-state hash-chained events. Fresh projects use workflow protocol2; existing projects record an explicit upgrade through owned reviewed work. Every task keeps its applicable protocol. New modules separate protocol/plan gates, role/debate orchestration and change/research/improvement governance while using the existing Project transaction, storage and projection mechanisms.

Protocol2 adds evidence-backed plans; major work adds a seven-field change request, two alternatives, role coverage and staged plan/result consensus plus independent approval. At least two independent reviewers participate. Registry capability labels are declarations; ownership/conflict history is retained. Consensus binds source/policy/task/assignment/capability/evidence, selects an actual analysis and preserves challenges/votes/dissent.

Research adds identified sources with honest access and coverage, seven-field ideas, distinct falsifiable hypotheses linked to experiments, and independent provisional novelty verdicts. Candidate claims require at least two distinct full-text sources and coverage evidence. Normal audit remains read-only; explicit improvement recording deduplicates proposed work without applying fixes or inventing root causes.

Use one master lifecycle with thin native product entries and subordinate `.agent/` worksheets. Package hidden/nested assets. A provider-neutral dispatch packet creates an integration boundary; actual independent provider dispatch remains a host/team responsibility.

## Impact and risks

Additional records increase state/event size and review effort. Deterministic roles may miss domain coverage. Frozen fingerprints can require renewed debate after meaningful changes; carefully exclude generated/self-referential inputs. Preserve old approval interpretation and old evidence bytes even when current scope changes produce historical warnings.

Local identities and capabilities are not authenticated. CLI gates cannot prevent direct edits, prove independence/comprehension or certify global novelty. There is no OS sandbox, external hash anchor, distributed consensus or automatically executed provider/service integration. Logical-day handover scenarios do not establish elapsed days or actual commercial-client use.

## Validation and recovery

Acceptance needs legacy regressions, new gate/round/staleness/access/migration checks, three executed software/research/switch scenarios, isolated wheel asset verification and Git reconstruction. Preserve immutable Phase1 event/evidence hashes and new failed attempts. Assess independent substantive challenges separately from scripted label-based controls.

Keep current project protocol/task state recoverable through the existing export/rebuild path. Projection repair regenerates views from valid authority and cannot fix corrupt ledger/evidence. Treat incomplete upgrade or changed input issues as recorded recovery work, not permission to rewrite historical events. See new Phase2 AUDIT evidence for executed results; this decision document does not claim unexecuted checks passed.

Revisit when actual provider dispatch, authenticated identities, distributed operation, large-history performance or deeper domain evidence is required. Split new integrations into reviewed ownership and validation scopes.

# UADOS v1.0 Phase 2 architecture

UADOS is a dependency-free Python 3.9+ local operating framework for project memory, acknowledged context, owned tasks, adversarial review, recorded experiments and protocol-versioned governance. It provides executable workflow gates and reusable maintained policies. It does not provision a hosted orchestration, authentication, CI or deployment service.

## Components

| Component | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `src/uados/cli.py` | Argument parsing, JSON outputs and process exit codes |
| `src/uados/project.py` | Initialization, mode detection, sessions, tasks, reviews, decisions, audit, export and reconstruction |
| `src/uados/storage.py` | Canonical hashing, SQLite authority, stable OS lock, atomic projection writes and project-relative evidence paths |
| `src/uados/context.py` | Markdown views, context manifest, Understanding Reports and fingerprints |
| `src/uados/research.py` | Experiment registration, provenance, execution, recovery and interpretation |
| `src/uados/protocol.py` | Workflow version, common runtime constants and Phase 2 projections |
| `src/uados/orchestration.py` | Capability registry, role generation/selection, dispatch packets and staged debate/consensus |
| `src/uados/governance.py` | Evidence-backed plans, change requests, research/novelty records and proposed improvements |
| `src/uados/assets/` | Maintained project scaffold: rules, memory guide, templates, prompts and examples |

Both `python -m uados` and the installed `uados` entry point dispatch to the same implementation. A source checkout can also use `python3 scripts/uados.py` without installation. `--project ROOT` precedes the command. Tracked-work operations take a session ID; read-only status/context operations do not. Initialization detects scaffold collisions; explicit `--adopt` preserves existing maintained instructions, reports them for integration and still rejects generated-state collisions.

## Authoritative state and projections

`.uados/ledger.sqlite3` contains one current-state row and an ordered event table. Each event records sequence, UTC timestamp, kind, actor label, summary, previous hash, complete resulting state and its SHA-256 hash. Canonical JSON uses stable key ordering and separators. A loader verifies SQLite consistency, contiguous sequences, every link/hash and equality between current state and the final event's state.

A mutation holds the stable project lock, begins an immediate SQLite transaction, verifies the existing record and generated views, checks workflow gates, applies the operation and commits the event plus current state together. The transaction is the durability boundary. After commit, UADOS updates generated files while retaining the same OS lock.

Generated Markdown, `.uados/state.json`, `.uados/events.jsonl` and session-report files are projections. Each file is written through a temporary file, flushed and replaced atomically; POSIX also synchronizes the parent directory. The group of projection files is not a separate atomic database transaction. If generation fails after commit, the action remains recorded and the CLI tells the contributor not to repeat it. `audit --repair` recreates views from the valid ledger.

The lock's inode is retained. POSIX uses `flock`; Windows uses a byte-range lock. Process exit releases the operating-system lock; a persistent lock file is expected and should not be removed to bypass contention. Locks serialize CLI activity, not arbitrary editor operations. Quiesce external writers when a stable evidence copy is required.

See [ADR 0001](adr/0001-local-ledger.md) for the storage decision and limitations. Full-state events simplify reconstruction but increase storage and verification cost with history; v1 favors transparent local correctness over large distributed histories.

## Context contract

The context bundle combines maintained project Markdown with generated views. Maintained inputs include root README/AGENTS/CLAUDE/workflow, `.agent/` protocols, Cursor wrappers, change policies, project memory, engineering rules, multi-agent policies, research policies, version-control/audit guidance and project `docs/`. Generated reports are excluded from the maintained scan to avoid self-reference. Templates and prompts are reusable supporting assets rather than a substitute for the governed policy files.

Starting a session emits and preserves a structured Understanding Report with objective, phase, architecture, completed work, blockers, risks, resource-document inventory, recommendations, decisions, failures and latest handover. The report has a content hash and records the context fingerprint. Its inventory does not verify hardware or external-data availability; contributors inspect and document those resources.

Acknowledgement must match the current issued report hash and current context. A contributor's own successful tracked mutation advances that session's context fingerprint. Other tracked work or maintained-context edits can make it stale; refresh replaces the report and clears acknowledgement until the new hash is acknowledged. Session-start/acknowledgement metadata is excluded from context-visible projections so acknowledgement does not invalidate itself.

This gate applies to CLI actions. It cannot force reading, prevent a direct edit or determine semantic comprehension. Generated-view edits are detected by projection comparison and require inspection/repair before tracked mutations continue.

## Task lifecycle and review

Tasks retain title, description/acceptance criteria, risk, scope, dependencies, author, implementer, owner session, lease, work submissions, evidence and reviews. Claims enforce completed dependencies and same-task ownership; explicit major scope is required. Active claims with overlapping declared paths, including directory/child relationships, are rejected. Scope-less routine tasks cannot provide file-level coordination, and arbitrary editors remain outside lease enforcement. Expired leases require a recorded takeover reason. Closing a session releases its unfinished task ownership and preserves a handover.

Routine completion requires an owned active task, a recorded explanation and unchanged validation evidence/scoped submission. Major tasks additionally require a current independent plan approval before claim and a current independent result approval before completion.

Review fingerprints include task specification, relevant engineering/multi-agent policy and scoped file snapshots. Result fingerprints additionally include submission revision, work and evidence. The review identity must differ from author and implementer. Evidence and current scope must remain consistent; new content requires renewed submission/review. The human team supplies an actually independent reviewer: agent labels do not authenticate identities.

Decisions preserve problem, at least two alternatives, selected action, reason, evidence and risk. A significant decision linked to an owned major task remains proposed until the independently reviewed task completes. Notes preserve technical explanations, lessons, failures and research reasoning without inventing a second source of task state.

## Research execution

An experiment records hypothesis, nonempty JSON argument array, configuration and dataset fingerprints, seed, required code scope and working directory. Before execution, the runner checks inputs and collects scoped hashes, optional Git revision, launcher Python/platform/package metadata and selected runtime environment variables. The seed is metadata; the invoked program must apply it. If a command launches a different interpreter or container, its environment needs its own emitted provenance.

The runner records durable execution intent, releases the lock, executes without an implicit shell, captures stdout/stderr and finalizes status/output evidence afterward. Other contributors can work while it runs. A successful process whose recorded inputs or scope changed during execution is invalidated. Timeouts and failures remain records. POSIX timeout cleanup addresses the process group; platform limitations must be considered for more complex subprocess trees.

Finalization resolves already recorded execution intent even if another contributor changed context during the run. The launcher session refreshes and acknowledges before subsequent tracked work. An orphaned `running` record is recovered with `experiment resolve` after the contributor inspects actual process state; the command records recovery and does not discover or terminate arbitrary processes. `experiment conclude` stores scientific interpretation and analysis evidence separately from operational exit status.

The runtime does not infer correct design, data completeness, statistical validity or novelty. Maintained research policies govern these responsibilities.

## Portability and recovery

`export PATH` requires a new directory outside the project. Under the project lock it copies a consistent SQLite backup, generated and maintained memory, recorded scopes/evidence/input/output artifacts and optional repeated `--include PATH` project-relative dependencies. The result is itself an initialized local project. It is a reproduction/context packet rather than an exhaustive image of the machine: unrelated files, external data, services and installed environments may need separate restoration.

For Git, preserve consistent `.uados/events.jsonl`, `.uados/state.json`, maintained/generated documents and required evidence. Keep the local SQLite database and lock out of normal text merges. After a clone without the database, `rebuild-ledger` validates the exported chain and state, reconstructs a missing database and regenerates projections. It never overwrites an existing ledger. Divergent event chains cannot be reconciled by concatenating or casually merging JSON lines; select a consistent history and record reconciliation work explicitly.

Audit distinguishes projection drift, missing/changed evidence, recorded warnings and ledger corruption. Repair is limited to projections. Missing/corrupt authoritative records need a validated reconstruction or trusted backup; missing evidence needs restoration or new validation. Fingerprints are local consistency evidence, not authenticated signatures against a trusted external anchor.

## Trust boundary

All collaborators are trusted local writers. The CLI's path rules reject project escapes and symlinked recorded resources, but experiment programs run with the user's privileges. Task leases are not a sandbox. A writer able to rewrite the whole database can also recompute its hash chain. Stronger identity, nonrepudiation, access control, external anchoring and distributed coordination require additional systems and an explicit future design.

## Contributor history and independent review

Claiming a task preserves the contributor identity across handovers. A task author or any current or previous implementation contributor cannot supply its independent plan or result approval. Changing sessions or handing implementation to another agent does not erase that conflict of interest. Reviewer labels still require trusted human attribution.


## Phase 2 governance boundary

Workflow protocol version is independent of SQLite schema version. Schema 1, the single transactional state/event authority and existing full-state events remain intact. Fresh initialization defaults to protocol 2. An explicit upgrade is recorded through an owned, independently planned legacy major task; its historical tasks retain their protocol and approvals. Old evidence, events and contributor history are not rewritten to simulate new compliance.

Protocol-2 tasks add a durable implementation/validation plan with evidence. Major tasks add a seven-field change request, at least two alternatives, generated role coverage and plan/result debates alongside independent plan/result approvals. The task's recorded protocol selects its gates. Missing protocol in historical state means the legacy interpretation, not an automatic migration.

Role generation is deterministic and uses project mode, task text and explicit task-type override. Task risk selects lifecycle depth rather than the role-generation heuristic. Registered capabilities are declarations. Selection covers roles with explicit contributor ownership and at least two eligible independent reviewers; roles may be combined transparently but one label cannot count twice toward independence. A provider-neutral dispatch packet carries task/context/instructions. The local framework does not invoke model providers or establish real independence.

Debates progress through independent analysis, adversarial challenge, votes and consensus. Each participant analyzes and challenges another participant; contribution records and round inputs are immutable. Consensus identifies an actual analysis, rejected alternatives, remaining risks and participant votes/challenges. Task/source/policy/evidence and assignment/capability fingerprints bind the proposal; result debate additionally binds submitted work. Generated consensus must not enter its own input hash. Stale inputs require renewed review, and dissent remains visible.

The research registry adds identified literature sources with truthful full-text/abstract/unavailable access, seven-field ideas and separate falsifiable hypotheses linked to experiments. Candidate novelty is provisional, requires at least two distinct full-text sources from distinct corpus groups plus coverage evidence, and needs an independent substantive audit. Overlap and inconclusive outcomes are preserved. A full-text flag does not establish search completeness, a valid experiment or publication acceptance.

Normal audit remains read-only. Explicit recording deduplicates proposed improvement records with problem, root cause (including unknown), improvement, implementation status and future prevention. It does not execute proposed fixes. Projection repair remains bounded to rebuilding views from valid authority.

Additional generated views are `CONSENSUS_DECISION.md`, `SYSTEM_IMPROVEMENT_LOG.md`, `MULTI_AGENT_SYSTEM/role_plans.md`, `CHANGE_REQUESTS/CR*.md` records, and research gap, novelty, decision and hypothesis registers. The maintained `CR_TEMPLATE.md` is not a generated change record. Generated files are excluded from maintained-policy fingerprints and ordinary source scope snapshots to avoid self-reference, but checked as projections by audit.

## Agent entry and recovery

`MASTER_AGENT_WORKFLOW.md` remains the single lifecycle authority. Root AGENTS and CLAUDE entry files and the actual Cursor `.mdc` wrapper refer to it. `.agent/` protocols provide operational worksheets; `.agent/compatibility.md` records official loader documentation and its limits. Referenced documents must be opened explicitly where the client does not import them. Compatibility files and hidden protocol directories are packaged scaffold assets and governed context inputs.

UADOS supports project-record recovery independently of the client. A logical Day 1/Day 30 identity-switch scenario validates reconstruction of decisions, status and remaining work; it is not evidence of elapsed wall-clock days or execution inside each named commercial product. Those integrations need their own real invocation evidence.

See [ADR 0002](adr/0002-phase2-governance.md) for the additive design and alternatives. Accepted limitations remain local cooperative identity, no OS sandbox, no distributed scheduling/consensus, no authenticated external hash anchor and full-state history growth. Verify hosted OS/CI and native-client results before expanding platform claims.


## Evidence snapshots and audit scope

New evidence registration reads exact bytes once and stores an immutable content-addressed copy under `.uados/evidence/sha256/`. Live approval gates validate both the referenced source path and its promised snapshot: retaining an original does not authorize an edited current input. Existing objects are verified and never overwritten. Orphan objects from rejected transactions are harmless unreferenced residue. Archive paths are excluded from implementation scope and retained in export and Git reconstruction.

Audit reports `ok` for current task/governance bindings and all promised snapshot integrity, and separately reports `history_ok`, `archived_originals` and `historical_evidence_drift`. Superseded records remain visible and are inspected across the event history. If old evidence predates snapshots and its original bytes have been overwritten, audit reports an unrecoverable historical warning rather than inventing a replacement. An unavailable or corrupt promised snapshot is an integrity error. A passing current audit does not mean every legacy original was preserved.

# Requirements and acceptance model

This implementation follows the supplied UADOS v1.0 Part 1 request and its Phase 2 extension. The operating framework combines local executable gates with maintained human/agent policies. The table distinguishes mechanisms from responsibilities that cannot be established by a local CLI alone.

| Requirement | Implemented mechanism | Acceptance evidence or review |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Context before action | Issued Understanding Report, exact hash acknowledgement and current context checks before tracked work | Unacknowledged, incorrect-hash and changed-policy operations are rejected; refresh permits an informed restart |
| Agent-independent project memory | Project-local SQLite ledger, Markdown/JSON views, decisions, notes and handovers | A second session recovers objective, decisions, failures, blockers and next actions without earlier chat |
| Documentation as development | Explained task result, evidence requirement, maintained architecture and research/policy templates | Completion without a work submission/evidence is rejected; reviewers assess explanatory adequacy |
| Reasoned important decisions | Structured ADR fields with at least two alternatives, reason, evidence and risk; major-task linkage | Decision records preserve rationale and significant linked decisions await reviewed task completion |
| Adversarial multi-agent review | Distinct contributor labels, challenged plan/result records, fingerprints and scope ownership | Major claim/completion without relevant independent approval is rejected; team verifies real independence |
| Software/research/hybrid modes | Evidence-based initialization heuristic and explicit override, common lifecycle plus research execution | Software/research evidence selects the expected mode; empty projects default to software with low confidence |
| Reproducible research | Registered argument vector, config/data/code fingerprints, seed metadata, launcher provenance, outputs and separate interpretation | Recorded execution and analysis can be inspected; researchers supply missing environment/data/design information |
| Extensible workflow | Maintained rules, extension template, rationale and context invalidation for governed policy edits | A policy change makes an existing session stale; new automation is separately implemented and validated |
| Long-term portability | Consistent local export and validated missing-ledger reconstruction from exported event history | The copied/reconstructed project passes audit and preserves task/decision/note history |
| Integrity and recovery | One authoritative ACID ledger, hash chain, stable lock, atomic view writes, audit and limited projection repair | Projection failure remains repairable without repeating committed work; altered evidence is not “repaired” by rewriting views |
| Required project structure | Packaged maintained assets and generated state views | Initialization creates every required directory and readable entry point without overwriting existing project files |

## Required project components

Initialization provides `README.md`, `MASTER_AGENT_WORKFLOW.md`, `PROJECT_MEMORY/`, `ENGINEERING_RULES/`, `MULTI_AGENT_SYSTEM/`, `RESEARCH_MANAGEMENT/`, `VERSION_CONTROL/`, `AUDIT/`, `TEMPLATES/`, `PROMPTS/` and `EXAMPLES/`. It additionally provides `AGENTS.md` and generated state/history/decision/handover records. Scaffold templates describe what to fill with project facts; generated registers start honestly empty.

Without `--adopt`, an existing target containing colliding scaffold files is rejected rather than overwritten. `init --adopt` preserves existing maintained files such as README, AGENTS and architecture documents, reports `preserved_files`, and fills missing maintained components. Contributors must inspect and integrate preserved onboarding instructions. Collisions with generated views still fail; adoption never silently replaces a previous generated state or a maintained instruction.

## Acceptance scenarios

1. **New project:** Install the package, initialize a clean target, inspect mode-detection evidence, start a session, read its report and acknowledge the exact hash.
2. **Routine task:** Define acceptance criteria, scope and dependencies; claim, implement, run meaningful validation, record evidence and complete. An unsatisfied dependency, conflicting active declared scope or missing evidence prevents the relevant action.
3. **Major task:** Record a plan; use an actually independent contributor for a challenged plan review; refresh implementer context and claim; submit results; review their current contents independently; refresh and complete. Self-review or stale scoped evidence is rejected.
4. **Agent switch:** Record a failure, reasoned decision and next action, close the session, then start another contributor's session. The replacement report and project files preserve the needed context.
5. **Research run:** Register an explicit hypothesis and input/code packet, run it with a timeout, inspect captured output, refresh and record an evidence-backed interpretation with uncertainty. Exit success alone is not a scientific result.
6. **Interrupted generation:** Simulate a projection failure after a commit. Audit finds projection drift; repair rebuilds from the ledger and the event remains recorded exactly once.
7. **Portability:** Export to a new external directory; audit and inspect it. Separately remove the local database only in a disposable copy and reconstruct from validated events to model a Git clone.
8. **Policy extension:** Edit a governed policy, observe stale-context rejection, then inspect and acknowledge the refreshed report. Verify any claimed new automated check separately.

Automated coverage lives in `tests/test_workflows.py`; the project's final verification report records which checks were actually executed. Maintained policies also require substantive reviewer judgment: tests cannot prove honesty, comprehension, novelty or independent identity.

Source-repository executable walkthroughs are in `scripts/run_examples.py`, covering software, research and hybrid operation. `scripts/verify_scaffold.py` checks scaffold completeness. Their scripted agent labels exercise CLI identity gates; they are not proof that the example's reviewer was a separate person or model.

## Operational scope

The v1 runtime uses Python's standard library and local storage. There are no provider/API keys, background services or network features. Git revision capture is optional and does not make Git a runtime dependency for ordinary project work.

The framework provides architecture, quality, security, data, literature, publication and release guidance. It does not automatically set up hosted CI/CD, cloud accounts, identity systems, protected branches, statistical analysis, instruments or a literature-search service. Those capabilities are extension/integration responsibilities with explicit project authorization and verification.

The local ledger cannot prevent direct file edits, establish a contributor's identity, prove an acknowledgement represents reading, resist a malicious writer who rewrites all hashes, or guarantee preservation without backups. These are explicit trust-boundary limitations, not claims hidden behind the term “enterprise.”


## Phase 2 requirements and acceptance

| Requirement | Executable mechanism | Evidence needed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Formal agent runtime | Stable sessions, issued Understanding Report, exact acknowledgement and evidence-backed task plan | Unacknowledged/stale work and missing protocol-2 plans rejected; startup packet preserved |
| Additive migration | Explicit protocol-2 enablement, schema1 ledger retained, per-task protocol interpretation | Baseline event hashes and Phase1 evidence unchanged; legacy tasks remain completable under their gates |
| Dynamic role generation | Task/mode-based coverage and registered declared capability selection | Software/research role variants, uncovered capabilities and assignment ownership exercised |
| Real adversarial process | Ordered analysis/challenge/vote/consensus, fixed participants, at least two independent reviewers | Missing rounds, self-review, unsupported selection, dissent and stale input paths rejected; substantive independent review supplied separately |
| Enterprise change control | Task-linked seven-field requests, two alternatives and readable evidence | Claim rejected without required major records and approvals; generated CR record agrees with ledger |
| Innovation audit | Source IDs/access, seven-field ideas, falsifiable hypotheses and independent provisional verdicts | Unavailable/abstract-only/duplicate-source coverage cannot support candidate; overlap/inconclusive retained |
| Reproducible experiment links | Idea/hypothesis associations plus existing command/input/environment provenance | Linked run, interpretation and recovery distinguish operational failure from scientific negative findings |
| Shared client authority | Thin AGENTS/CLAUDE and Cursor `.mdc` entry files with explicit master reading | Hidden/nested assets included in installed wheel; references consistent; native product execution claims require separate evidence |
| Self-improvement | Audit stays read-only by default; explicit deduplicated proposed improvement records | Repeat finding does not create uncontrolled duplicates or execute fixes; unknown cause remains explicit |
| Long-term recovery | Rich handover/context and preserved ledger contributor history | Incoming identity reconstructs status, decisions and unfinished work without previous chat |

Additional initialized components include `.agent/`, `CHANGE_REQUESTS/`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursor/rules/uados.md` and the actual loader wrapper `.cursor/rules/uados.mdc`. Role, consensus, change, improvement, literature-gap, novelty, research-decision and hypothesis views are generated from ledger state rather than copied as maintained fixtures.

The Phase 2 scenario runner must execute a new software project with startup/planning/review/memory updates, a research project with literature/hypothesis/experiment/novelty records, and an outgoing/incoming agent handover under logical Day 1/Day 30 labels. These are real local CLI/state exercises with simulated commercial-client identities; report exact commands, assertions and failures. Model dispatch is manual and the scenarios cannot authenticate model identity or prove 30 elapsed days.

Preserve `AUDIT/scenario_test_report.md`, `AUDIT/phase2-final-report.md` and `AUDIT/self_review.md` as new evidence. Final assessment covers modularity/extensibility/maintenance, startup/context/role capability, documentation/testing/consistency, reproducibility and innovation analysis. Self-review asks whether new contributors can recover context, collaborate and trace decisions, what actually executes, and what weaknesses remain. Packaging tests must exercise an isolated installed wheel including hidden rules; Git reconstruction must retain current registry/evidence records.

Platform/product claims remain bounded to executed evidence. Local checks cannot prove honesty, native-client obedience, capability competence, actual contributor independence, global novelty, instrumentation validity or distributed reliability.

# Optional signed ledger checkpoints

Phase 3 adds `trust checkpoint` and `trust verify` alongside the existing local
ledger. SQLite schema 1, workflow protocol 2, legacy events, audits and task gates
retain their meaning. The runtime still uses the Python standard library;
these optional commands require OpenSSH `ssh-keygen` with SSHSIG support.

## Operator trust contract

An operator owns the signing key, exact signer principal, allowed-signers policy,
optional revoked-keys/KRL file and the latest checkpoint SHA256 pin. All paths
must be outside the project, without symlinks or `..`. Keep keys and policy/pins
in an independently protected location. UADOS never enrolls a key, generates a
production key, copies private keys into evidence or authenticates agent labels.

Store the returned digest through a trusted channel outside this workspace.
Passing a digest read from the same attacker-controlled bundle supplies no
independent anchor. The allowed-signers policy authorizes a principal/key and may
restrict its namespace; an authorized signature is more than an unvalidated
signature-structure check. Key rotation is an operator action: update a versioned
external policy, use the new key, issue a new bundle, and distribute its new pin.
Revocation applies the supplied *current* policy, including an OpenSSH revoked
public-key list or KRL. Historical policy evaluation requires retaining and
explicitly choosing that policy externally; there is no trusted timestamp.

The fixed namespace is `uados-checkpoint@uados.local`. The payload binds format,
version, principal, first event hash (project identity), event sequence/head hash,
full-state digest and a signed audit assertion. It does not sign each contributor
action or authenticate model/provider independence.

## Create and verify

The paths below are illustrative external operator paths. Supply your existing
key and authorized policy; no key is created by these commands.

```sh
python3 scripts/uados.py --project . trust checkpoint \
  --output /secure/uados/checkpoint-001 --principal alice@example.org \
  --key /secure/keys/uados-signing
python3 scripts/uados.py --project . trust verify \
  --bundle /secure/uados/checkpoint-001 --principal alice@example.org \
  --expected-sha256 EXTERNALLY_TRUSTED_SHA256 \
  --allowed-signers /secure/policies/uados-allowed-signers \
  --revocations /secure/policies/uados-revoked-keys --require-current
```

Allowed-signers format is the standard OpenSSH format, for example:

```text
alice@example.org namespaces="uados-checkpoint@uados.local" ssh-ed25519 PUBLIC_KEY_BASE64
```

Creation performs the normal current audit, rejects failed current integrity,
then reacquires the existing project lock and requires the audit head/count to
match the loaded ledger. It holds the lock through signing and publication. An
intervening CLI mutation fails the capture instead of nesting locks or asserting
an inconsistent observation. Locks do not stop arbitrary editor/OS writes.

No ledger event is appended. A new external directory contains `checkpoint.json`,
`checkpoint.json.sig` and a final `COMPLETE` marker with both content hashes.
Signing succeeds in staging before exclusive directory creation. Concurrent
creators have one winner; an existing destination is never overwritten. If disk
publication fails after exclusive creation, the incomplete directory remains for
operator inspection and fails verification. Choose a new output path to retry.
Completion markers establish bundle completeness, not authorization.

Verification snapshots the exact supplied public policy/revocation and signature
bytes into a disposable private directory, verifies the authorized signature and
fixed namespace, parses strict canonical JSON and checks the externally pinned
digest against the exact message. It then validates the whole ledger hash chain
and matches the checkpoint's project/sequence/head/state to that event. Inputs
are size bounded; missing tools, malformed inputs, timeouts, wrong principals,
unauthorized/revoked keys and altered outputs produce explicit failure.

## Interpret the result

`signature_verified` and `ledger_binding_verified` describe the authorized
checkpoint and its ledger prefix. `covers_current_head` is false if valid later
events exist; `--require-current` rejects that case. A trusted newest external pin
rejects a truncated or rehashed local history. Replaying both an old legitimate
bundle *and its old trusted pin* against a truncated old workspace can succeed:
this tool cannot discover a globally latest head. Protect latest pins externally
when rollback resistance matters.

`signed_audit_assertion` records the signer's observation at creation. It cannot
independently recreate old live-file availability. `current_audit` is a separate
fresh audit; edited live evidence or projections can fail it even while the old
signature remains valid. Overall `ok` and CLI exit 0 require current audit
consistency. Current failure returns exit 1; input/authorization/binding failures
return exit 2. `history_ok=false` remains visible and does not fabricate missing
legacy originals. Historical loss is compatible with a passing current audit.

This optional integration provides a cryptographic checkpoint boundary under
operator-controlled external trust. It does not establish protected operating
system storage, organizational identity enrollment, global freshness, distributed
coordination, actual provider dispatch, hosted CI or scientific validity.

## Validation and reference

`python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -p test_trust.py -v` uses real temporary
Ed25519 signatures, authorization, revocation, rotation, namespace and tamper
checks; test keys live outside disposable fixture projects and are deleted.
Ledger forgery/truncation, historical-prefix handling, parser/path/size failures,
timeout/tool failure, audit capture races and concurrent output publication have
separate checks. A missing OpenSSH executable is reported as an explicit test
skip, not passing cryptographic validation; commands fail unavailable.

API reference: [official OpenBSD ssh-keygen manual](https://man.openbsd.org/ssh-keygen.1),
checked on 2026-10-13, including `-Y sign`, authorized `-Y verify`, namespaces,
allowed-signers policies and `-r` revocations. Host behavior is verified by
executed tests separately from this reference.
